📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major update, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of newly introduced content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

According to recent reports, the first fresh arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Speaking of elemental reactions, fresh in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a significant confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the new Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

In a recent development, the first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a latest outfit in the shop at a discount.

According to recent reports, version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

All around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

Finally, you can look forward to the latest Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

Planning to Stop Taking a GLP-1? Here’s How to Maintain Weight Loss

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Switching GLP-1 medications or undergoing bariatric surgery may help people maintain greater weight loss than stopping treatment entirely, according to a newly introduced study presented at ObesityWeek and published in eClinicalMedicine on November 14.
  • The Cleveland Clinic study compared five strategies for managing weight after treatment with GLP-1 medications, analyzing data from 20,486 adults with obesity or type 2 diabetes.
  • People who stop taking GLP-1 medications often regain weight.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Switching GLP-1 medications or undergoing bariatric surgery may help people maintain greater weight loss than stopping treatment entirely, according to a newly introduced study presented at ObesityWeek and published in eClinicalMedicine on November 14.

The Cleveland Clinic study compared five strategies for managing weight after treatment with GLP-1 medications, analyzing data from 20,486 adults with obesity or type 2 diabetes.

People who stop taking GLP-1 medications often regain weight. Researchers examined whether continuing treatment, switching medications, or undergoing bariatric surgery could help limit weight regain or support further weight loss.

The findings showed that people who underwent bariatric surgery or switched between semaglutide (Ozempic) and tirzepatide (Zepbound) experienced the greatest overall weight loss.

Industry observers note that the study participants had an average age of 56.7 years, an average weight of 109 kg (240.3 lbs), and an average body mass index (BMI) of 38. All had been taking either semaglutide or tirzepatide for at least 90 days.

The researchers categorized the participants into five groups:.

After 2 years, those who underwent bariatric surgery saw an average loss of 28.2% of their body weight or about 31.5 kg (69.4 lbs).

“We increasingly view medications and surgery as complementary tools rather than competing ones,” said Mir Ali, MD, medical director of MemorialCare Surgical Weight Loss Center at Orange Coast Medical Center in Fountain Valley, CA, who wasn’t involved in the study.

“For patients with severe obesity (typically a BMI of 35 or higher, or 30+ with metabolic conditions like type 2 diabetes), bariatric surgery remains the most durable, cost-effective intervention available,” he added. “Using a GLP-1 beforehand can safely reduce liver volume and lower surgical risk, while surgery provides the permanent anatomical and hormonal reset needed to maintain that weight loss long-term without relying indefinitely on weekly injections.”.

During the same period, those who switched between semaglutide and tirzepatide lost 16% of their body weight, or about 18 kg (39.6 lbs).

Sources indicate that participants who switched from semaglutide to tirzepatide lost 3 kg (6.6 lbs) more than those who continued taking semaglutide. However, participants already taking tirzepatide lost 4.5 kg (9.9 lbs) more by continuing treatment rather than switching to semaglutide.

The other groups experienced lower amounts of weight loss:.

After one year, participants with type 2 diabetes experienced HbA1c reductions of 1.76% following bariatric surgery, 1.43% after switching GLP-1 medications, and 1.32% after continuing their original medication, compared with 0.48% among those who discontinued treatment entirely.

After one year, participants with hypertension (high blood pressure) also experienced greater reductions in blood pressure following surgery or switching GLP-1 medications than those who discontinued treatment entirely.

“[This study] reinforces the need for a long term, multi-modal continuum of care rather than treating GLP-1s as a temporary fix,” stated Ali.

Ali also recommended the following strategies to help maintain weight loss after stopping a GLP-1 medication:.

The findings highlight the importance of having a long-term weight management proposal in place before stopping a GLP-1 medication.

In a recent development, before stopping a GLP-1 medication, talk with a healthcare professional. They can help you explore your options and determine which strategies may be most appropriate for your health needs.

Industry observers note that ali told Healthline that identifying the reason for stopping treatment is an notable first step. He noted that people often discontinue GLP-1 medications because of gastrointestinal side effects, supply problems, or loss of insurance coverage rather than because they no longer need treatment.

He noted that if side effects are the glitch, adjusting the dose or switching to a different agent often solves the problem.

According to recent reports, ali also emphasized that stopping a GLP-1 medication shouldn’t be viewed as a test of willpower. Increased hunger after discontinuing treatment is a biological response, not a personal failure.

“Have a concrete ‘off-ramp’ proposal in place with your doctor before taking your last dose, so you have medical, nutritional, or surgical support ready to protect the health gains you worked hard to achieve,” advised Ali.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When discussing a car’s performance in the snow, it all comes down to tires and clearance. Tires are the only part of your vehicle that makes contact with the road, so the rubber mounted on your car is the number-one determiner of how much grip you’ll have while accelerating, turning, or braking on slippery surfaces such as snow and ice. All-wheel drive may help you get going in the snow, but it doesn’t help you stop.

So, when selecting this list of best vehicles for snow, we included only top-rated models that come standard from the factory with tires rated for severe snow service. These tires are marked with the all-important three-peak mountain snowflake icon (3PMSF). This icon is found on either all-weather tires or all-terrain tires that have been tested and are capable of at least 110 percent of the traction of a reference all-season tire. Not every all-terrain tire carries this marking.

Sources indicate that it’s also vital to mention that any car with winter tires would be our preferred method of transportation in snowy conditions. If you don’t want to pony up for one of these SUVs or trucks with their often pricey optional off-road packages that include the 3PMSF tires, consider outfitting a different vehicle with winter tires. Check out our Winter Tire Buying Guide for advice on which tires to choose.

According to recent reports, the CX-50 is one of our favorite compact SUVs, and it offers a rugged-looking trim level called the Meridian Edition. This version comes with snow-rated all-terrain tires no matter whether you choose the naturally aspirated 2.5 S Meridian Edition or the more powerful Turbo Meridian Edition.

Tire: General Grabber A/T or Pirelli Scorpion XTM A/T.

If you’re not willing to go all out for the Raptor version of the F-150 found later on this list, this popular pickup truck also offers a lesser off-road trim level that also comes with snow-rated tires. The F-150 Tremor doesn’t have the upgraded engine or suspension from the Raptor, but it does have style upgrades and other modifications compared with the standard F-150. There are two factory tire choices, either General or Pirelli, but both have the 3PMSF icon.

Many versions of the Ram 1500 pickup offer an Off-Road Group option package that includes Falken Wildpeak all-terrain tires in various sizes, all of which have the 3PMSF icon. Ironically enough, the Ram’s most off-road-oriented versions—the Rebel, RHO, and TRX—also have all-terrain tires, but not ones specifically rated for snow.

Recent findings suggest that the GX is closely related to the Toyota Land Cruiser and is the most off-road-ready SUV in the Lexus lineup. To get snow-rated tires from the factory, you have to opt for the Overtrail model, which comes with all-terrain tires and other upgrades meant to improve the GX’s performance in the dirt and other types of off-road terrain. It has an impressive 9.8 inches of ground clearance.

Ford Ranger Raptor, Ford F-150 Raptor, Ford Bronco Raptor.

Tire: BFGoodrich All-Terrain T/A K02 and K03.

Recent findings suggest that the BFGoodrich K0 series of off-road tires is well regarded among off-road enthusiasts. Ford’s Raptor off-road pickups, the Ranger and F-150, come with the latest K03 tires, while the Bronco Raptor SUV comes with K02s. We’re fans of all of these high-performance 4x4s, but the Ranger Raptor is our favorite of the bunch due to its smaller size, lower base price, and subdued styling.

Subaru has offered standard all-wheel drive on nearly all of its models for quite a while now, which has earned it a reputation for all-weather performance. But not every Subaru comes with tires optimized for snow. Only the Wilderness version of the Outback mid-size SUV comes with Yokohama Geolandar All-Terrain tires that carry this rating. (The Forester Wilderness and Crosstrek Wilderness also have these tires, but those models don’t rate as high in our testing.).

Mercedes-Benz G550 with G Professional Package.

No, you probably don’t need a G-wagen to traipse through a few inches of snow to get to the grocery store. But this highly capable SUV has become a style icon for its distinctive aesthetic, and for good reason. The most capable version of the G-class is the G550 with the G Professional package, which adds all-terrain tires, a roof rack, a bull bar on the front, and other off-road upgrades.

Ford Mustang Mach-E Trail and Rally.

The Mustang Mach-E compact electric SUV is one of the few vehicles you can get from the factory with all-weather tires, in this case the Michelin CrossClimate2. These snow-rated tires come on certain versions of the Mach-E, including the high-performance, 480-hp Rally and the new-for-2027 Trail (pictured), which also has extra ground clearance.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, the first attempt at a rescue was unsuccessful.
  • The roughly 70-pound turtle is now receiving behind-the-scenes care at the Aquarium of the Pacific.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in July, a green sea turtle (Chelonia mydas) found itself in a bind. Like many unlucky marine and aquatic animals, this turtle ended up tangled in fishing line. But this reptile’s luck was about to change. Volunteers with the Aquarium of the Pacific’s Southern California Sea Turtle Monitoring community science program were out gathering field data on the green sea turtles spotted in the San Gabriel River in Santa Barbra, California.

In a recent development, the first attempt at a rescue was unsuccessful. The sea turtle was swimming in deep water with low visibility, so it could not be reached. But by the next day, the team saw the turtle swimming in an area of the river easier to access.

The roughly 70-pound turtle is now receiving behind-the-scenes care at the Aquarium of the Pacific. According to the aquarium, the fishing line caused a severe constriction injury on its the sea turtle’s left flipper. The reptile also swallowed some of the fishing line, risking damage to its internal organs.

“When the sea turtle came to us, it had a fishing line constriction that caused severe damage to its flipper,” Aquarium of the Pacific veterinarian Dr. Brittany Stevens noted in an emailed statement. “Despite all efforts over the past few months, unfortunately, the left flipper could not be saved and had to be amputated to aid in the turtle’s recovery.”.

This is not the aquarium’s first experience with three-flippered turtles. The team rescued and rehabilitated a green sea turtle named Porkchop, who was released into the wild in February. Porkchop has since been spotted by aquarium volunteers who monitor sea turtles.

The turtle now named Endor is receiving wound care and antibiotics as it goes through rehabilitation, with the goal of eventually returning to the wild. Endor is a sub-adult, meaning it is past the juvenile stage, and approaching sexual maturity, but not yet a full adult turtle. The sex has not been determined and Endor was previously tagged by NOAA in 2025.

Recent findings suggest that as Endor is rehabilitated, it will eventually move from the behind-the-scenes sea turtle care area to a rehabilitation area open for public viewing. Meatloaf, an over 250-pound rescued green sea turtle, is right now living in that space.

The Aquarium of the Pacific has been caring for several turtle species since 2000, including green, olive ridley (Lepidochelys olivacea), and loggerhead (Caretta caretta). All sea turtle species found in U.S. waters are listed as endangered or threatened and are protected by the Endangered Species Act.

To find a licensed animal rescue and rehabilitation organization in your area, visit Animal Help Now or call your local animal control department.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that correcting yourself while parking isn't an abnormal event.
  • Because that's how many times one Chinese EV was caught on security camera footage trying to find the perfect parking spot overnight.
  • An apparently empty Avatr EV was caught on camera spending the majority of the night maneuvering around marked parking spaces in a parking structure in China's Anhui Province.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that correcting yourself while parking isn't an abnormal event. Maybe you overshot the turn and pulled just a little bit too close to the car next to you. So you back out, adjust, and try again. It's not all that embarrassing—at least not the first time. But how many times does it have to happen before you start to go red in the face (or just give up and drive away)?

Recent findings suggest that two? Five? What about 868? Because that's how many times one Chinese EV was caught on security camera footage trying to find the perfect parking spot overnight.

An apparently empty Avatr EV was caught on camera spending the majority of the night maneuvering around marked parking spaces in a parking structure in China's Anhui Province. The car can be seen on video moving around a small area of the garage. Reversing into a space, pulling forward, repositioning, and doing it all over again.

Watching the footage is a bit confusing. If you know that it's a car with parking assist or other autonomy features, you probably assume that the car is just having trouble deciding how well it's parked—like it's some sort of programming error that makes the car's software lack confidence that its parking job is good enough. That may not have been the case here.

It turns out that this particular car wasn't alone in its parking shenanigans. In fact, other video footage soon emerged showing other Avatr and Huajing-branded cars pulling off similar parking stunts.

While the exact reasoning for the repeated parking is unknown, CarNewsChina rapidly put together that the cars in the videos all sport Huawei's driver assistance software.

It has been revealed that the footage emerged just as a contest run by Huawei was taking place. It ran through November 13th and was meant to show off the capabilities of the tech firm's Qiankun Intelligent Driving system by giving people points in eight different categories depending on how they used vehicles' Qiankun-backed features while driving.

One of these categories is called "Parking Elite." It measures the use of Automatic Parking Assist, Exit-and-Park Assist, Parking Lot Navigation Assist, and Remote Parking Assist to assign points to drivers. The top 100 drivers would receive Huawei points, which can be redeemed for in-app purchases and discounts.

Sources indicate that of course, this reportedly led to some drivers attempting to game the system. CarNewsChina even surfaces a post where one driver claims to have completed 1,000 parking sessions in a single day. It's worth noting that Huawei's tech is technically a driver-assistance feature and not an autonomous driving function; the car is supposed to always have a human supervising these types of actions.

These are just theories, of course, but the claims from drivers and security camera footage do seem like gaming the system is a plausible explanation.

According to recent reports, either way, you have to admit that if you saw a car parking itself 868 times overnight into various parking spaces, you'd wonder what was going on—I know I would. At least it's good for a laugh and didn't cause a traffic jam.

We’ve all watched dogs or cats twitch their ears and paws as they contentedly sleep away the day. And it turns out that black bears (Ursus americanus) have adorable sleeptime spasms, too—as one small black bear named ‘Nugget’ demonstrated in a video captured at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska.

In honor of his endearing, jerk-filled sleep, the U.S. Forest Service team at Tongass National Forest has awarded Nugget the Biggest Dreamer Award. Nugget was seen peacefully snoozing on a rock with his head resting on one of his giant paws as flies flit around his face.

“With ears and nose twitching away, Nugget was off in what seemed to be a very pleasant dreamland,” the rangers write. “Does watching make you wonder what he’s dreaming about? It must be salmon, right?”.

According to recent reports, the rangers have already awarded Nugget two other awards this year, including the Annoying Sibling Award and the Introvert Award. He may just receive the most awards of any Anan Creek bear in the forest! Go Nugget!

It has been revealed that nugget is easy to spot among the bears who frequent the salmon-filled Anan Creek. He’s a bit smaller and has fur that changes from a tufty red in spring to sleek black coat in autumn. His unique coloring also makes it look like he has goggles around his eyes. Rangers named him Nugget in 2024, and he’s been seen at Anan Creek ever since.

It has been revealed that as Nugget snoozed alongside the burbling water, other black and brown bears came and went as they had their fill of salmon. As the rangers write, his tranquil sleep among the other bears is “a testament to the amazing ecosystem at Anan Wildlife Observatory.”.

Industry observers note that despite his three awards, Nugget is far the only bear (or mink!) getting awards this season. Tongass National Forest’s rangers are awarding the annual Anan Bear Awards to the dozens of bears spotted at the Anan Wildlife Observatory in Alaska this past summer.

The largest national forest in the United States, Tongass covers most of southeastern Alaska, including the state’s capital city of Juneau. The area also includes Mendenhall Glacier (a popular destination for Alaskan cruises), hiking trails, eagles soaring above, and—of course—plenty of bears.

According to recent reports, one of the bear hotspots in the forest is Anan Creek. The creek has one of the largest runs of pink salmon in Southeast Alaska, making it a popular dinner spot among black and brown bears.

According to recent reports, according to Friends of Anan, 39 bears are known to feast on the salmon at Anan Creek. The population includes 31 black bears and eight brown bears (Ursus arctos). Similar to their more portly counterparts farther to the north in Katmai National Park, the bears return each summer to feast at the creek and teach their cubs how to fish in order to survive. And like the fat bears of Katmai, every bear at Anan Creek has their own behaviors and quirks.

The U.S. Forest Service tracks and documents every bear spotted at Anan, while explore.org’s cameras broadcast live streams of their behavior. Tune in next year to decide who ought to win the Biggest Dreamer award next!

Used EVs spend 25.2 percent less time on the market than gasoline vehicles, while hybrids spend 10.7 percent less time on the market than gasoline models.

The Tesla Cybertruck leads the rankings at 39.1 days on the market, selling in 26.4 fewer days than the average used pickup. The Ford Maverick hybrid ranks second at 43.3 days, followed by the fully electric Rivian R1T at 45.2 days and the Ford F-150 Lightning at 47.4 days.

According to recent reports, gasoline-powered trucks account for five of the top 10 positions, led by the Toyota Tacoma in fifth place at 50.1 days. The Ford Maverick hybrid ranks second, outperforming all electric trucks except the Cybertruck.

EVs also perform strongly in the broader used market, per iSeeCars, where they claim 16 of the 25 fastest-selling model rankings.

The Audi A4 Allroad is the fastest-selling used vehicle overall, averaging just over a month on the market, or 33.7 days, followed by the Lexus RX 450h+ plug-in hybrid at 35.0 days and Audi Q4 Sportback e-tron at 36.3 days.

Industry observers note that what are the slowest sellers on the used car market? Two additional electric vehicles appear among the slowest-selling models: the electric Dodge Charger, averaging 98.2 days, and the GMC Hummer EV SUV, averaging 84.9 days.

In a recent development, “There’s clearly a big shift from latest to used status for electric vehicles, especially when fuel prices have remained elevated for several months,” remarked Brauer. “Used shoppers are all about value, which normally plays against electric vehicles. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In the classic Thanksgiving comedy Planes, Trains and Automobiles, hapless hero Del Griffith (played by the late, great John Candy) delivers an emotional riposte to Steve Martin’s uptight ad man Neal Page that stands as a beautifully dignified defense of kindness, empathy and self-love in the face of his own perceived shortcomings.

“You want to hurt me? Go right ahead if it makes you feel any better…I could be a cold, hard cynic like you. But I don’t like to hurt people’s feelings. You think what you want about me, I’m not changing. I… I like me. My wife likes me…because I’m the real article. What you see is what you get.”.

For many of us around the holidays, particularly after a night of excess, Del and Neal’s exchange could read as our internal monologue – your kinder inner voice battling the internal bully who judges your every overindulgence. The jury’s out on whether the kind voice is ever as potent as Del’s is in that moment. But it should be, because when it comes to your health around the holidays, the bully has usually got it wrong.

The truth is, for most of us, one day of immoderation during Thanksgiving is unlikely to matter in the grand scheme. As such, you would do well to avoid the litany of holiday season health myths out there, many of which seem hell-bent on punishing you for taking a day off:.

Like all misinformation, these kinds of medical myths are loud and tend to die hard, but they almost always trade on quick fixes that target the wrong thing.

It has been revealed that A 2020 review of 23 observational studies found that most highlighted significant weight gain during festive periods, averaging roughly a pound and a half. One of the original studies, a landmark NIH study from 2000, found that much of that weight tends to stick around. So the question is not what you ate on Thanksgiving Thursday and how quickly you can “undo the damage,” but rather whether the extended holiday season becomes a two-month period where your healthy routine goes out the window. Some things to look out for on that front:.

It has been revealed that none of this is a free pass for everyone. If you manage a health condition, you likely have less margin for error, even when talking about a single meal or a drink. Critical factors include timing, sodium intake, alcohol intake, and missed medication. A few non-exhaustive examples:.

Whatever condition you’re managing, the move for all of them remains the same – be prepared. Check your plan with your care team before the holiday, not after, and call them if something feels off afterward.

Industry observers note that technically, feeling good on Black Friday starts on Thursday. A short and light walk after a feast can help smooth out post-meal blood sugar – the earlier the better, ideally within an hour of eating. Staying upright for a couple of hours to help with digestion, particularly if you’re prone to reflux, is also a great idea. If you’re on medication, remember to take it on time. And, at the risk of sounding prudish, and this goes for everyone: try to get to bed at a sensible hour.

Above all else, Thanksgiving is a holiday built around gratitude and kindness, so channel your inner Del Griffith and remember to be both grateful and kind, to yourself and to those around you – evidence suggests that’s also good for your health.

Robin Hough is the Editor-in-Chief of Healthline, and in addition to this regular Letter from the Editor column, he can be found every other Wednesday in our Healthline Wellness Wire newsletter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

If you’ve ever looked at a classic 1929 Bentley Blower and thought, “That looks great, but could it be smaller, electric, and somehow still cost six figures?” then good news: your car has arrived.

Hedley Studios has completed the first 25 production Bentley Blower Jnrs, with the hand-built electric mini-cars now heading to customers. Deliveries are beginning in the UK before expanding across Europe.

The Blower Jnr is an officially licensed collaboration with Bentley, recreating the famous 1929 Bentley 4½ Liter Supercharged Team Car No. 2 at 85% scale. Unlike many scaled-down collector cars, though, this isn’t merely an expensive toy for cruising around your estate. It’s actually road legal.

In a recent development, in the UK and EU, the Blower Jnr is homologated as an L7e quadricycle, reaching over 50 mph (80 km/h) and offering a certified 75-mile (120 km) range. A separate US program is also planned, though it’s not clear exactly what classification the mini-EV would receive stateside.

It has been revealed that underneath the delightfully old-school bodywork is a decidedly newer 48V electric drivetrain producing 31 hp (23 kW). The electric motor sits across the rear axle, while batteries and power electronics are packaged underneath the car.

The carbon-fiber tub rides on a steel frame with leaf springs and period-style friction dampers, while Brembo disc brakes handle stopping duties up front.

Every car that people ever loved will come back in some electric version that they can actually drive and love.

Recent findings suggest that there are some particularly fun details, too. The charging port is hidden inside a recreation of the original Bentley’s supercharger housing, while modern necessities like indicators, headlights, and even a reversing camera have been incorporated without ruining the 1929 aesthetic.

The first 25 cars are part of a nearly sold-out run of 99 First Editions. Another 250 configurable cars will follow, bringing total production to just 349 units.

Sources indicate that and “Jnr” definitely doesn’t mean junior pricing. Configurable cars start at £112,500 before taxes – roughly $148,000 at current exchange rates.

Then again, if you’re buying a hand-built miniature electric Bentley, value probably wasn’t the first thing on your mind.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that ghostly blue clouds about 6,800 light-years from Earth are all that remain of an ancient cosmic demise. These and other details are visible in the most recent look at a supernova remnant classified as SNR G295.5+09.7. Depending on how you see it, SNR G295.5+09.7 likely earns at least one of its nicknames: the Betta Fish or Mermaid Nebula.

In a recent development, A supernova remnant encompasses vast swirling waves of dust, gas, and stellar material created in the wake of a star’s death. SNR G295.5+09.7 exploded between 7,000 and 10,000 years ago in the Centaurus constellation, ejecting its outer layers of matter to collide with interstellar space’s own gases. The energy from these interactions subsequently caused the region to glow, which is now detectable by highly sensitive instruments. In this case, astronomers imaged the Betta Fish nebula using the 570-megapixel Dark Energy Camera (DECam) located at the Cerro Tololo Inter-American Observatory (CTIO) in Chile.

Although impossible to see with the naked eye, the supernova remnant contains the last vestige of its prior life in the form of a neutron star. The incredibly, miniscule dense object is what’s left from a star that was once multiple times the mass as our sun. Even now, SNR G295.5+09.7’s neutron star is larger than the solar system’s anchor—cramming about 1.4 times the sun’s into a sphere barely 12-miles in diameter. As the National Science Foundation’s National Optical-Infrared Astronomy Research Laboratory noted in its announcement, the stellar object is so small that it could fit inside the city of Tucson, Arizona.

Industry observers note that however, the Betta Fish Nebula almost never happened. If the dynamics were slightly different, the massive stellar object’s collapse could have generated a black hole instead of a neutron star. If that were the case, the glowing swirls of cosmic material would likely never escape the black hole’s unfathomable gravitational pull.

New York Claims 'Enough Is Enough' To In-Car Subscriptions

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, if you ask the auto industry, subscriptions are the future.
  • It has been revealed that A newly introduced law aims to put a stop to many forms of in-car subscriptions and after-sale purchases, meaning that if all it takes is a credit card number to switch on a feature after you buy the car, it probably isn't going to fly in New York State.
  • According to recent reports, governor Kathy Hochul signed into law a bill that prohibits automakers, dealerships, and third-party providers from charging car buyers ongoing subscription fees in certain cases.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, if you ask the auto industry, subscriptions are the future. Consumers might disagree. They don't want basic features like heated seats being locked behind a paywall, especially when the hardware is already installed. Legislators in Upcoming York have decided those types of subscriptions are nothing more than a money grab.

It has been revealed that A newly introduced law aims to put a stop to many forms of in-car subscriptions and after-sale purchases, meaning that if all it takes is a credit card number to switch on a feature after you buy the car, it probably isn't going to fly in New York State. But there are, of course, some exclusions.

According to recent reports, governor Kathy Hochul signed into law a bill that prohibits automakers, dealerships, and third-party providers from charging car buyers ongoing subscription fees in certain cases. Specifically, it prohibits recurring fees for hardware already installed in the car at the time of purchase, so long as those features don't create an ongoing cost for the manufacturer or a provider.

A snippet from the State's announcement claims it best (and uses the infamous heated seat subscription as a prime example):.

Amid rising consumer prices, the new law guards against a rising trend of car companies charging car owners fees to activate and use built-in features like heated seats, enhanced navigation, hands-free driving and entertainment options that do not present an ongoing expense for dealers and manufacturers.

There are, of course, provisions in the legislation of what features aren't covered by the subscription freeze.

New York indicates that driver assistance and automation features, connected cellular services, in-car hotspot, satellite radio, vehicle telematics, roadside assistance, navigation updates, and infotainment features are some of the items excluded from protection under the new legislation.

Sources indicate that notably, that means Tesla can continue charging for features like Full Self-Driving. It does, however, call into question features like Acceleration Boost, which is a $2,000 software-based performance upgrade that requires no extra ongoing costs.

This distinction tracks fairly in line with what both enthusiasts and consumers have been shouting at their phone screens for the last few years. If it's local hardware that's already installed in the vehicle and requires no ongoing costs to maintain (like heated seats, climate control, or remote start using a physical key fob), it feels like a cash grab to continue to charge owners after purchasing the vehicle. Things that cost money to provide—like internet-connected streaming features or driver assistance features that are being actively developed and upgraded over the air—are a bit more defensible.

If your $70,000 SUV still needs its manufacturer's servers, cellular network, fresh maps with to-the-minute traffic conditions, and continuously updated self-driving software—you might not get out of paying a monthly fee. But if it just needs a relay flipped on to work completely offline, then the manufacturer better just work it into the cost.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

As recently revealed, the new experience introduces today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside update 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

In a recent development, the beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the plan is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

Sources indicate that the Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as swiftly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

Industry observers note that the Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

The Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two fresh additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.

#132530. Tech Report: The Most Valuable Hot Wheels Cars Ever

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Caranddriver ↗ Open Full Page

Tech Report: The Most Valuable Hot Wheels Cars Ever

📅 21 Dec 2018 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1340 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Caranddriver

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Collecting cars is expensive, time-consuming, and something of a game of patience.
  • Recent findings suggest that to get a sense of where the market is at right now and where it’s going, we caught up with Hot Wheels uber-collector Bruce Pascal.
  • Before diving in on the spendy stuff, Pascal was quick to note that the Hot Wheels collecting hobby is as broad as it is deep.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Collecting cars is expensive, time-consuming, and something of a game of patience. Collecting little die-cast cars is mostly just the latter two. However, at the top end of the game, rare and hard-to-find Hot Wheels can command prices that raise eyebrows.

Recent findings suggest that to get a sense of where the market is at right now and where it’s going, we caught up with Hot Wheels uber-collector Bruce Pascal. Pascal has thousands of die-cast cars in his collection, which even extends to the full-size classic hot rod “King T,” which inspired the 1968 Hot Wheels Hot Heap. Together, the collection is worth over a million dollars, and it includes an example of the most valuable Hot Wheels of them all, the one at the bottom of this list.

Before diving in on the spendy stuff, Pascal was quick to note that the Hot Wheels collecting hobby is as broad as it is deep. He notes that while eBay used to be where auction battles raised prices higher, about half of all transactions these days occur on Facebook fan pages, with regular auctions, Deal or No Deal style haggling, and sometimes even other Hot Wheels fans throwing some cash on the table to help someone else lock down a buy of a car that perhaps had sentimental value.

You can find most of these places by identifying your segment of interest in Hot Wheels, whether that's the “Redline” cars of the 1960s and 1970s, “Blackwall later cars,” or just plain typing in “Hot Wheels” for everything. Pascal notes that the vast majority of transactions are for less than $10, so feel free to wheel and deal as you build up your own toy car collection. They’re a lot easier to find parking for than a full-size one. Meantime, here’s a look at the Hot Wheels that fetch the most money when they change hands.

2026 Red Line Club Ferrari F40 - $120–$150.

Values of the full-size Ferrari F40 have more than doubled over the past few years, making owning one a multimillion-dollar payout. If you’d invested on a smaller scale, you could have doubled your money too. Mattel’s Red Line Club costs under 10 bucks a year and opens up access to highly detailed die-casts for members only. The RLC F40 debuted in August for $50, and examples are now trading for as much as triple that on eBay. It's not nearly the same money as the 1960s cars, but it indicates that anyone can get into the Hot Wheels collecting game.

1974 Magenta Rodger Dodger with White Interior – $3000.

First issued in 1974, Rodger Dodgers with a black interior are relatively common; those with the white-colored interior are rare, as pictured here, and are the ones that collectors desire.

1968 Brown Custom Camaro – $3000–$5000.

Industry observers note that the Chevrolet Camaro is probably the most Hot Wheels of Hot Wheels, right out of the gate as one of the original 16 castings produced. Brown over a white interior is among the rarest combinations, although values on these haven't really changed much over the past few years.

Rare Hot Wheels Prototype Camaro Worth $100,000.

1972 Pink Superfine Turbine – $3500–$4500.

Sources indicate that designed by Larry Wood, the Superfine Turbine design dates from the early 1970s and has remained fairly stable in price recently. Wood joined Hot Wheels back in 1969 and was with the company for 50 years, collaborating with the likes of Ed “Substantial Daddy” Roth and George Barris.

Sources indicate that another Hot Wheels flight of fancy and designed by Paul Tam, the Open Fire is a stretched-out AMC Gremlin with six wheels and plenty of motor. This little green goblin is rare, but prices have held steady of late.

1969 Red Baron with White Interior – $4500–$5000.

With its German helmet theme, the Red Baron incorporates a bit of 1960s biker culture and has been reissued many times. This original one, with the rare white interior, is the collector’s choice.

Industry observers note that datsun’s 240Z got some respect right out of the gate in the early 1970s, but fans had to wait until 1977 for Hot Wheels to get its first imported car model. These have doubled in price since 2019.

1974 Blue Rodger Dodger – $6000.

Industry observers note that A hopped-up Mopar with flames, the Rodger Dodger was built in low quantities with blue paint. The rarity drives the price up, as it has also doubled in value over the years.

1971 Spectraflame Purple Bye Focal – $6000.

Industry observers note that bye Focal was Mattel’s term for a range of colors in the 1970s, and this purple was the rarest of them. The twin hood scoops are a nice touch, but this model has an Achilles’ heel where the body will begin to fall apart. That just makes surviving examples more rare.

1969 Cheetah Base with Python Body – $6000.

In a recent development, this example is a prototype Hot Wheels, one that escaped into the wild even though it wasn’t meant to. The production model was intended to be called the Python, but the original in-house name was the Cheetah. Since only a handful of cars were built with the early base plate on them, that makes this model valuable.

1968 Pink Beatnik Bandit – $6000 (in package, $20,000).

Based on an Ed Roth hot rod, the Beatnik Bandit was another of the first Sweet Sixteen original Hot Wheels. The casting came in nearly 20 colors, but the pink shade is the rarest and thus the most sought after. Prices have remained pretty steady, though an example still in the original packaging fetched five figures recently.

1970 Red Ferrari 312P with White Interior – $7000.

Almost every example of this Ferrari model produced came with a black plastic interior. This casting has the white interior that collectors obsess over finding.

1968 White Custom Camaro – $8000.

Said to be the very first Hot Wheels to make production, the white version of the original run Custom Camaro was supposedly meant to be a blank canvas for designers. Add flames? Chrome-look paint? By mistake, some of these cars were packaged up and sent out, finding their way to the public.

1971 Red Olds 442 with Black Interior – $8000.

According to recent reports, another model unusual for its color combination, the Olds 442 casting almost never came in red over black. It’s rumored that fewer than 15 surviving examples of these cars right now exist.

1976 Porsche 917 Super Chrome – $8000.

Sources indicate that A relative newcomer to the ultra-collectible Hot Wheels segment, this 917 sprang up the charts thanks to its combo of bright paint and association with Porsche. Even Hot Wheels isn’t immune from the air-cooled Porsche boom.

Industry observers note that everyone loves a Woody wagon, but Hot Wheels didn't make many of them in 1969. Again, rarity drives the price point.

1969 Ed Shaver Blue AMX – $10,000.

According to recent reports, A U.K. import, this AMX was made as part of a sponsorship deal with drag racer Ed Shaver. Hot Wheels made lots of AMX castings, so the critical thing is finding one with the original side decals—and making sure they’re the genuine item.

1969 Brown Custom Charger – $13,000.

The actual valuation on this little brown Mopar is actually something of a question mark. It’s rare though the casting was very popular, as Hot Wheels didn’t make many examples with brown paint. However, none have changed hands recently, so the actual auction price for one could be much higher.

1969 Mad Maverick Base on Mighty Maverick – $15,000.

According to recent reports, considered to be one of the rarest production Redline Hot Wheels, this purple 442 has steadily increased in price recently to break into the top five of the most valuable Hot Wheels. It was made exclusively in Mattel’s Hong Kong facilities for just a single year.

#132529. The 2027 Toyota GRMN Corolla Is Almost Worth the Squeeze

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1127 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Roadandtrack ↗ Open Full Page

The 2027 Toyota GRMN Corolla Is Almost Worth the Squeeze

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1127 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Roadandtrack

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Toyota’s GR Corolla has valiantly filled the gap left by the deceased Subaru WRX STI and Mitsubishi Lancer Evo as a rally-inspired compact that combines everyday usability with performance.
  • But how does it fare if practicality is reduced to sharpen the driving experience?
  • Industry observers note that limited to 730 units, the 2027 Toyota GRMN Corolla’s upgrades are primarily focused on improved dynamic response.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toyota’s GR Corolla has valiantly filled the gap left by the deceased Subaru WRX STI and Mitsubishi Lancer Evo as a rally-inspired compact that combines everyday usability with performance. Combining a torque-rich turbocharged three-cylinder with a manual transmission and all-wheel drive in a practical four-door shell still sounds like a winning formula to us.

But how does it fare if practicality is reduced to sharpen the driving experience? When Toyota unveiled a limited run of track-focused GR Corollas with no back seat and a $65,655 price tag, alongside some choice mechanical upgrades, the first reaction was skepticism. Why dilute the approachable, jack-of-all-trades appeal of the existing GR Corolla with a more expensive version? To answer that, Toyota took Road & Track to Eagles Canyon Raceway on the outskirts of Dallas, Texas, for the chance to give the GRMN Corolla a proper romp around the track. I’m happy to report that the special edition offered a compelling defense.

Industry observers note that limited to 730 units, the 2027 Toyota GRMN Corolla’s upgrades are primarily focused on improved dynamic response. The suspension, tuned at the Nürburgring and Fuji Speedway, gets shorter, stiffer bump stops up front and longer bump stops in the rear to better deal with circuit curbing and midcorner bumps. Toyota has also firmed up the steering weight, especially at high speeds, and revised front-end aerodynamics to better vent turbulent air through upcoming flaps in the wheel wells and carbon-fiber hood. Wider Michelin Cup 2 tires are also standard, replacing the GR’s Pilot Sport 4s. Driven hard on the elevation-heavy road course, the GRMN felt much more confident and able.

Part of the GR Corolla’s handling charm has historically been its rally-car rowdiness—a tendency to roll and then set into a corner, plus some degree of rear-end playfulness under power and braking—and the revised suspension setup manages to maintain this character. Approaching Turn 12, a descending, off-camber sweeper where the correct line takes the front end over an elevated curb, the GRMN Corolla refused to be unsettled. Similarly, the tendency to swing out the lightened rear end under braking I remember well from the GR Corolla seemed largely negated and easier to correct when it did happen.

Recent findings suggest that the front end of the GRMN Corolla was also sharper than ever, with a rapid turn-in and heavier, confidence-inspiring steering weight. Leaning into Turn 6 at wide-open throttle, the front end didn’t waver as I asked for more steering angle at nearly 100 mph. There was even steering feel, which is a treat on any modern performance car. However, rapid steering changes were sometimes accompanied by a binding feeling, a trait we’ve experienced in previous GR Corolla variants. It was hard to say whether the aerodynamic upgrades contributed to the solid front end, but the addition of the grippier tires no doubt played a significant part in the improved confidence. Back-to-back laps in a standard GR Corolla on Pilot Sport 4s tires proved the GRMN was more planted and offered much better communication of its position and limitations.

Toyota has only made small changes to the 1.6-liter turbocharged inline-three in the GRMN, adding just 7 lb-ft of torque to take the total to 302 lb-ft, accompanied by an unchanged 300 hp. Response felt improved off the line, and there was more top-end grunt too, although the biggest reason for the perception of additional surge was likely the newly introduced revised-ratio six-speed manual transmission, which is exclusive to the GRMN.

In a recent development, with a longer first gear and shorter third gear, the car found a good middle ground between the slightly-too-shortness of the STI and the excessive length of something like a Porsche 718. For reference, fourth gear runs out at 105 mph, a good compromise between the thrill of changing gears and having to do so too often. The upcoming, slightly smaller shift knob also felt more ergonomic in my hand, and the updated shifter-cable mount offered more satisfying action.

Of course, a core part of the appeal of the regular GR Corolla is its tunable differential, and this is carried over unchanged on the GRMN. Track mode offered the most rear-biased power split, allowing 70 percent to be sent to the back axle, while Gravel mode split power evenly between both axles. Even in the rear-biased setting, the GRMN Corolla was more liable to push the front end on power than rotate the rear end around.

In a recent development, I actually preferred the GRMN Corolla in Gravel mode around Eagles Canyon Raceway, as the front-wheel-biased performance best practice of trail braking and on-throttle patience more easily led to a clean lap. Brake feel was also improved on the GRMN Corolla, with the GRMN exhibiting no fade over more than half a dozen laps, and there was always more power available through the pedal when asked.

In a recent development, ergonomically, the GRMN Corolla remains a sneakily competent sports car trapped in a four-door hatchback shape. With new bucket-style seats in red and black upholstery, the GRMN Corolla offered more lateral support at the expense of comfort. For me, the new seats felt thinner and decidedly less comfortable than the set in the standard GR Corolla. Even so, the driving position is low enough and well placed for pedal and shifter access. The pedal box was also spaced for easy heel-toe downshifts, though the intelligent throttle-blipping downshift assistance system means a driver doesn’t need to do this. Similarly, the lack of rear seats didn’t add any obvious level of noise intrusion, although the 66-pound omission came at obvious cost to carrying capacity. All told, the GRMN Corolla improves on the standard GR Corolla formula in nearly every dynamic way, but does that make it worth the premium?

Recent findings suggest that at $65,655, the GRMN Corolla is a hard sell for the average enthusiast buyer. Sure, it is the best-driving GR Corolla yet—they should all come from the factory in this configuration—but it doesn’t have particularly inspiring acceleration nor mind-numbing on-track performance. Its best feature is pure agility, but even rear-driven sports machines like the venerable $65,395 Cadillac CT4-V Blackwing or the $69,550 BMW M2 offer plenty of hustle these days. Sure, there are few modern performance road cars that could outrun the GRMN Corolla on a gravel track, but that’s not a strong enough use case to sway the typical enthusiast buyer away from more horsepower and bigger engines.

Recent findings suggest that regardless, the GRMN has already proved itself well priced considering the warmth of the response it has so far received from enthusiasts, many seeking to upgrade from the GR Corolla. They will likely snap up every unit, regardless of markup. And they will be happy.

NIO targets 10,000 battery swap stations and $52B in batteries by 2030

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1162 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • NIO says its energy arm, NIO Power, will operate more than 10,000 battery swap stations and manage over RMB 350 billion ($52 billion) worth of battery packs by 2030.
  • Recent findings suggest that that’s more than double the swap network NIO runs in China today.
  • Sources indicate that NIO shared the targets today at NIO IN 2026, its annual technology event, held in Guangzhou to mark the firm’s 12th anniversary.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

NIO says its energy arm, NIO Power, will operate more than 10,000 battery swap stations and manage over RMB 350 billion ($52 billion) worth of battery packs by 2030.

Recent findings suggest that that’s more than double the swap network NIO runs in China today. And it comes from a firm that already missed its last big swap station target.

Sources indicate that NIO shared the targets today at NIO IN 2026, its annual technology event, held in Guangzhou to mark the firm’s 12th anniversary. NIO Power also expects to deliver over 10 billion kWh of energy per year through charging and battery swapping by the end of the decade.

As of November 11, NIO had 4,252 battery swap stations in China, alongside 5,584 charging stations, according to the company’s latest network count.

Getting to 10,000 by 2030 means adding roughly 1,400 swap stations per year for four straight years. NIO added 679 in 2024 and 681 in 2025. So the fresh plan needs about double the firm’s recent pace.

It has been revealed that even this year’s goal of “at least 1,000” new stations looks tight. NIO had 3,729 swap stations in February when it celebrated its 100 millionth swap, which means it has added just over 500 since then.

There’s also some history here. At its 2021 Power Day, NIO committed to more than 4,000 battery swap stations worldwide by the end of 2025, with about 1,000 of them outside China. By February 2026, it had about 3,700, almost all of them in China.

The energy target is just as aggressive. NIO’s swap network had delivered 5.28 billion kWh in total by February, after roughly eight years of operation. The 2030 goal is nearly twice that every year, although it also counts NIO’s charging stations.

Sources indicate that NIO’s swap network is tied to its Battery-as-a-Service (BaaS) model, where customers can buy the car without the pack and rent the battery instead. That means someone has to own a massive fleet of packs, both in customers’ cars and sitting charged in stations. NIO says it wants to manage more than $52 billion of them in four years.

For context, NIO reported total revenue of about $4.7 billion in Q2 2026.

Sources indicate that NIO has been moving the heavy capital off its own books. Under deals like its agreement with Zhongan Energy to build 500 swap stations within a year, partners own the stations while NIO handles the technology and operations. NIO Power notes it has now co-built more than 900 swap stations with partners.

Recent findings suggest that the hardware is also getting better. NIO opened its first fifth-generation swap stations in August, and they’re the first to serve all three of its brands. That includes the compact firefly, which couldn’t use older stations because of its shorter wheelbase.

NIO CFO Stanley Qu, who also heads NIO Power, presented the unit as NIO’s showcase for running a business with AI agents, using them to manage battery value, station operations, and energy efficiency.

The swap targets were only part of the event; everything else focused on NIO’s AI-fication.

NIO also launched NIO WorldModel (NWM) 3.0, the latest version of its driver-assist AI, which starts rolling out in December to vehicles with the Banyan, Cedar, Cedar S, and Coconut+ systems, pending regulatory clearance.

NIO indicates NWM 3.0 needs 40% fewer driver interventions than the previous version. It didn’t say how many interventions it started from, which makes the number hard to evaluate. It also claims a roughly 60% boost in drivers’ “sense of reassurance,” whatever that means.

The more concrete claims are about speed: NIO says overall vehicle control latency is down 54% and chassis control latency is down 78%, while training is five times more efficient.

NIO also unveiled NOMI Intelligence 4.0, a rebuild of its in-car assistant around an AI agent framework that can initiative and carry out tasks on its own instead of following set commands. The first release, Cedar 2.0.0, will be filed in early December. Cars on Cedar S and Banyan should get it in Q2 2027, followed later by ONVO models.

Sources indicate that finally, CEO William Li pitched NIO as an “AI-native organization.” He argued the global auto industry is worth $7 to $9 trillion and that AI could add more than $1.2 trillion in value to it. NIO says it has deployed over 7,500 AI agents internally, with more than 2.9 million executions so far.

Recent findings suggest that NIO’s swap network is real, and it works. The organization passed 130 million swaps this month, and nobody else has built anything close at this scale. Tesla sort of tried battery swapping and quietly dropped it. NIO kept going.

Sources indicate that BYD charges in 5 to 9 minutes. a swap takes 5 minutes. I don't know man. It doesn't look good for NIO.

But 10,000 stations by 2030 requires a build pace NIO has never hit, and its last swap target slipped badly. So we’d treat that number as an ambition, not a forecast.

The $52 billion battery figure is the interesting part. It shows what NIO Power really is: a battery asset manager that also builds stations. That only works if partners keep putting up the capital and the batteries keep earning money over their lifetime. NIO has been trying to get other automakers on board for years, with limited results – though it appears to be starting to attract more players.

And the competition isn’t standing still. Chinese automakers like BYD are pushing megawatt-level charging that adds hundreds of kilometers of range in about the time it takes to swap a battery. If ultra-fast charging becomes common, NIO’s swap advantage gets a lot thinner.

Sources indicate that battery swapping is one way to recharge in minutes, but if you drive an EV, charging at home on solar power is still the cheapest way to fuel it. With electricity rates up almost 10% last year and expected to keep climbing, going solar is one of the best ways to protect yourself against rising costs. #132527. Two-Thirds of Dementia Content On TikTok Is Misleading, Researchers Say

Two-Thirds of Dementia Content On TikTok Is Misleading, Researchers Say

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1025 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A fresh survey suggests that about two-thirds of dementia advice videos on TikTok are misleading.
  • Of the videos examined, the analysis shows that nearly half contained inaccurate and potentially damaging information.
  • The researchers say that approximately 44% of TikTok creators who share dementia content lack credibility and appropriate qualifications.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A fresh survey suggests that about two-thirds of dementia advice videos on TikTok are misleading.

Of the videos examined, the analysis shows that nearly half contained inaccurate and potentially damaging information.

The researchers say that approximately 44% of TikTok creators who share dementia content lack credibility and appropriate qualifications.

Although misleading dementia content may appear on other social media platforms, this research examined only TikTok content, warranting further investigation.

The survey was commissioned by Homewatch Caregivers and has not been published in a peer-reviewed scientific journal.

It has been revealed that A spokesperson for TikTok told Healthline that if health-related content is potentially harmful, it is flagged for removal. The spokesperson added that 99.6% of misinformation deemed violative was proactively removed from the platform in 2026.

The spokesperson added that TikTok relies on fact-checking and guidance from public health authorities to help assess the accuracy of content. The platform may also apply warning labels to content that cannot be verified as accurate.

Looking to social media for health information is not uncommon. A recent poll reports that 31% of adults in the United States use social media at least once a month to look for health information and advice.

Experts advise seeking information about dementia from trusted sources, such as a primary care doctor and organizations like the National Institute on Aging (NIA) and the Alzheimer’s Association, rather than social media, where content creators who share advice often lack expertise.

“It’s normal to want answers quickly when you’re caring for someone living with dementia, and a short video from someone who seems to know what they’re talking about can be really convincing,” noted lead researcher Jennifer Winarski, senior manager of care operations and quality for Homewatch CareGivers.

It has been revealed that “Despite there being some genuinely helpful information out there, you don’t always know whether it’s backed by medical evidence, so we wanted to bring our own expertise to uncover whether popular TikToks can be trusted,” she told Healthline. “We hope our report will encourage people to be a bit more careful about what they act on.”.

For the survey, researchers selected a sample of 500 of the most-watched dementia-related videos on TikTok with hashtags such as:.

Researchers then transcribed the video data to assess its accuracy.

According to recent reports, the researchers found that two-thirds (66.4%) of the popular TikTok videos contained misleading information. Of those videos, about half (47.6%) contained potentially damaging misleading dementia information.

“It’s clear that many of the creators mean well, but much of what we saw was personal opinion rather than proven information, and in a few cases, general good health tips were presented as if they were specifically helpful for individuals living with dementia,” Winarski said.

“If families act on that, they could end up spending time and money on things that won’t help — and in the worst of cases, it could delay getting the support their loved one really needs,” she added.

Industry observers note that dung Trinh, MD, an internist for MemorialCare Medical Group and chief medical officer of the Healthy Brain Clinic in Irvine, CA, stated it’s important to be aware of the volume of misleading dementia information on social media. Trinh was not involved in this survey.

Some people may be making decisions about their health based on incomplete, misleading, or incorrect information, he stated.

“For example, someone might see a video claiming that a particular supplement can reverse Alzheimer’s disease or that certain memory problems automatically mean someone has dementia,” Trinh said.

“These messages can lead to unnecessary fear, false reassurance, wasted money, or delays in getting a proper diagnosis.”.

“We are entering an exciting era in Alzheimer’s care, with advances in blood-based biomarkers, earlier detection, and treatments that may slow disease progression in appropriately selected patients,” Trinh continued.

“Getting an accurate diagnosis and receiving timely medical guidance are becoming increasingly notable.”.

Sources indicate that the researchers examined the content creators behind the TikTok videos included in their analysis. They found that 44% of video creators behind the misleading videos had no relevant qualifications.

Rehan Aziz, MD, vice chair of education in the Department of Psychiatry at Hackensack Meridian Jersey Shore University Medical Center and associate professor of psychiatry and neurology at the Hackensack Meridian School of Medicine in New Jersey, said that content creators offering dementia advice should have relevant qualifications. Aziz wasn’t involved in the survey.

“Start by looking at the creator’s profile for a full name and a specific credential, such as MD, DO, PhD, or RN, along with a specialty,” Aziz told Healthline.

“For dementia, the most relevant experts include neurologists, geriatric psychiatrists, geriatricians, neuropsychologists, and nurses, including advanced practice nurses, or social workers who specialize in dementia care.”.

“You can confirm a doctor’s license through your state’s licensing board website and check board certification at certificationmatters.org,” Aziz noted.

As of 2020, more than 55 million people worldwide were living with dementia — a neurological condition that negatively affects the brain. Researchers predict this number will hit 78 million by 2030.

The increase in the number of people seeking dementia content online is a reflection of this trend.

It has been revealed that when looking for accurate dementia information and guidance, Nestor Beltre, MD, a neurologist with Baptist Health Kenneth C. Griffin Neuroscience Institute, part of Baptist Health South Florida, remarked a great first step is to speak with their primary care physician. Beltre wasn’t involved in the survey.

“Memory changes can occur for many different reasons, and some causes, including vitamin deficiencies, depression, and certain medical conditions, may be treatable,” he told Healthline.

“Early evaluation can help identify what may be contributing to these changes and determine the most appropriate next steps. Depending on the individual’s symptoms, a neurologist, psychiatrist, or neuropsychologist can provide further evaluation and guidance,” Belter continued.

Beltre advised turning to trusted resources such as the Alzheimer’s Association and the National Institute on Aging, which can increase public understanding of memory-related conditions and available treatment options.

“The most important message is that patients and families have resources available to help them better understand and manage cognitive health,” he said.
