General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Popsci ↗ Open Full Page

Industry News: Meteorites fascinated ancient Egyptians—just look at King Tut’s ‘space dagger’

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1343 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In August 2026, an analysis of iron from ancient Greek tombs revealed surprising results.
  • Sources indicate that it seems that, among the upper classes of Bronze Age Greece, rings fashioned from this out-of-this-world metal were all the rage.
  • Researchers believe that the Greek meteoric rings were actually imported from Egypt: a land with a special relationship to this metal from the skies.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In August 2026, an analysis of iron from ancient Greek tombs revealed surprising results. The objects surveyed included weapons and jewelry from around 3,000 to 4,000 years ago. Most of them were fashioned from regular old iron ore, but around 10 rings were made of iron from outer space—aka from meteorites that crash-landed on Earth.

Sources indicate that it seems that, among the upper classes of Bronze Age Greece, rings fashioned from this out-of-this-world metal were all the rage. Before people learned how to extract iron from ore by melting it at super-high temperatures—a process called smelting—the only source of metallic iron was the occasional space rock. This material, known as meteoric iron, is rare worldwide, but especially in Greece, where approaching meteors usually disappear into the sea rather than make landfall.

Researchers believe that the Greek meteoric rings were actually imported from Egypt: a land with a special relationship to this metal from the skies.

It has been revealed that meteoric iron can be identified because it’s purer than the iron ore that naturally occurs on Earth, with a higher proportion of nickel mixed into it. Because meteoric iron “already arrives on Earth in metallic form,” says Victoria Almansa-Villatoro, a professor of Egyptology at Yale University, “it’s very malleable” and can be shaped more easily than unrefined ore.

It has been revealed that the Egyptians started working with this rare material early. “The oldest meteoric iron objects in the world come from Egypt,” states Almansa-Villatoro: Nine small beads, excavated from a site called Gerzeh along the bank of the Nile about 20 miles south of Cairo, are the oldest artifacts discovered made from space rocks. They are dated to around 3,200 BCE, more than a thousand years older than the 10 meteoric iron rings found in Greece.

Not only are the Gerzeh beads older than any other meteoric iron objects, they are much, much older than widespread iron smelting in Egypt. Almansa-Villatoro explains that “Egypt was relatively late in comparison with other Near Eastern civilizations to start smelting iron.” By the time the Egyptians were producing iron on a large scale in the 500s BCE, ancient people in Anatolia and other regions had been doing it for about five hundred years.

It has been revealed that A major reason for this late adoption was Egypt’s natural resources. Iron smelting forges burned a lot of wood charcoal, and Egypt had no large forests. For centuries, the Egyptians relied on bronze, which cost less fuel to produce. It wasn’t until major changes in political and trade networks, including pressure to match the iron arsenals of foreign enemies like the Assyrians, that the Egyptians finally made the shift.

According to recent reports, while early iron weapons and armor were not automatically better than bronze ones, iron proved easier to repair, and could be strengthened through further reworking. But objects like the Gerzeh beads show that the ancient Egyptians shaped small amounts of meteoric iron long before they knew how to extract it from ore.

The Gerzeh iron beads were incorporated into jewelry with gems and gold, hinting at their perceived value. All of the other Egyptian objects believed to be made of meteoric iron are similarly small and mostly decorative. The largest and most spectacular is a dagger with a meteoric iron blade more than eight inches long. It was found in the tomb of Egypt’s famous pharaoh, Tutankhamun, who died around 1,323 BCE.

Government records from the reign of Tutankhamun’s grandfather, Amenhotep III, mention an Anatolian king gifting a dagger to the Pharaoh. “People have speculated that this was the same dagger,” claims Almansa-Villatoro. “Because, why would they make such a substantial deal about this king receiving a dagger from a foreign leader, unless it’s made of a very vital or very rare material?” As seen with the recent findings from Greece, demand for meteoric iron in the ancient Mediterranean was international.

As of 2013, archaeologists had discovered 28 objects in Egypt believed to be made of meteoric iron. This accounts for about half of the 55 known ancient meteoric iron artifacts found across Europe, Asia, and Africa as of 2023.

The prevalence of meteoric iron in Egypt is difficult to determine, as the composition of many iron objects has never been evaluated. Additionally, indicates Almansa-Villatoro, “we find more things in Egypt in general from this time period than in other regions,” due to the long history of archaeology there.

Sources indicate that analysis has shown that some of the Egyptian meteoric iron objects are made from several small meteorites combined. This might suggest that the Egyptians were “harvesting” and “actively looking” for this rare material, notes Almansa-Villatoro, rather than just using it at random when a meteorite happened to land nearby.

Almansa-Villatoro believes that meteoric iron “was valuable because it was recognized to be material that came from the sky,” not just because it was more pure than other iron. Ancient Egyptian religious texts link iron with the heavens and the spiritual realm of the gods, who were sometimes described as having iron bones. One Egyptian term for iron literally translates to “the iron of the sky.“.

“Some tools made of meteoric iron were used in a very important funerary ritual known as ‘the Opening of the Mouth,’” indicates Almansa-Villatoro. These include small iron blades found in Tutankhamun’s tomb (though not the famous dagger). The purpose of this ritual was “to give the deceased back their senses,” Almansa-Villatoro explains, allowing them to speak, breathe, and eat in the afterlife. Meteoric iron might have been particularly prized for crafting these ritual objects.

By the time of Tutankhamun’s reign, the Egyptians might have encountered smelted iron produced in other lands, but they were still using meteoric iron in rituals and reverently placing it in tombs.

“It is possible that they still saw meteoric iron as something different” from smelted iron, says Almansa-Villatoro, though it’s hard to say for sure.

Ancient Greece’s most famous oracle was just high on gas fumes.

In medieval France, murderous pigs faced trial and execution.

Ancient Romans thought drinking gladiator blood could cure epilepsy.

At Scotland’s ancient Cladh Hallan, homes were full of human bones.

7 ways toilets have killed people.

For ancient Romans, pooping was a group activity.

In a recent development, some Egyptian texts describe a dome of water with an iron shell enclosing the Earth. Meteoric iron might have been explained as fragments of this cosmic shell breaking off and falling to the Earth.

According to recent reports, it’s clear that the Egyptians considered meteoric iron to be a special material, but what exactly they knew or didn’t know about it is not always easy to figure out. The Egyptians understood and interpreted the world around them using very different methods from our own. While we rely on experimental data documented in writing, ancient Egypt “was very much an oral society, where knowledge was transmitted through ritual and through recitation of texts,” notes Almansa-Villatoro.

In a recent development, in ancient Egypt, “things that we wouldn’t consider science nowadays, like myth, could have fulfilled the same function” as science does today, notes Almansa-Villatoro. The Egyptians used narrative myths to describe the physical universe. The iron shell surrounding the Earth appears in accounts of the soul’s journey to the afterlife, as a barrier that the spirits of the dead must sail across to reach the skies.

Industry observers note that with our modern knowledge, it’s easy to explain how a space rock might land on Earth. But what if all you knew of outer space was what you could see with your eyes from our planet’s surface? Egyptian myths may not have the structure of a modern scientific paper, but they offer a glimpse into how ancient people made sense of awe-inspiring natural phenomena like metal falling from the skies.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Louis Vuitton Horlogerie Tambour Automatic 40 mm in Rose Gold, $65,000, louisvuitton.com.

Inspiration can come from the most unlikely of sources. If any era could be defined by that fact, it would be the early Aughts. During this transitional period, watch brands young and old looked to establish themselves within an emerging luxury space, and they did so in wildly diverse and creative ways. Before the throwback trend took hold of the industry, design language was largely forward-looking with an emphasis on innovation and character. This was the scene in 2002, when Louis Vuitton entered the watch market with the unconventional Tambour, which has since served as the core of the brand’s efforts in this domain.

This story originally appeared in Volume 38 of Road & Track.

In a recent development, taking its name from the French word for “drum,” the original Tambour watch features towering walls that widen at the base and accept an integrated lug piece reminiscent of the brand’s luggage handles. A reverence to the craft is clear from subtle details such as the alignment of the Louis Vuitton letters along the side of the case matching each hour marker, the shape of the crown and pushers, and the articulation of the lug. The drumlike case remains unique to this day, and the Tambour template has proved surprisingly versatile, with Louis Vuitton expanding the collection into a range of styles.

The Tambour stands as a monument to the best elements of its formative era and remains one of the Aughts’ more enduring horological identities. Today’s modern iteration is a refined reflection of the same ideas that put Louis Vuitton on the timekeeping map nearly a quarter ­century ago. The funky Aughts freedom that allowed for the creation of the Tambour turned into a core strength for a 21st-century watchmaking powerhouse.

BMW is sending over-the-air software updates to roughly 16 million cars around the world, and American-spec vehicles running the latest iteration of the company’s operating system are getting a big improvement.

Recent findings suggest that starting in December, vehicles in the United States fitted with the Highway & Commuting Assistant running BMW’s Operating System X, which include the newly introduced iX3 and iX5, will be able to stop at red lights and automatically drive off again. The small but important change transforms BMW’s driver assistance feature into a stronger competitor to Tesla’s so-called Full Self-Driving (Supervised) system.

According to recent reports, the automatic stop-and-go at red lights functionality has been available in other markets, such as Germany, for a longer time, but it’s making its way to America now, too. According to BMW, the Highway & Commuting Assistant can automatically brake to a standstill, and when the light turns green, the vehicle will automatically set off again or prompt the driver to continue, as showcased in the video below.

Sources indicate that that’s not all, though. The December software enhancement brings a total of five new features, as well as improvements to 19 existing functions. Most have to do with driver assistance, navigation, charging, infotainment, and comfort, and cars running BMW Operating System 8.5, 9, and X are covered.

It has been revealed that some of the latest features include Google Maps Places data in BMW Maps for cars running Operating System 9 and X, as well as Amazon Prime Video for all Operating System X cars, plus the 1 Series, 2 Series Active Tourer, X1, and X3. Predicted occupancy for public chargers, based on historical data, is also being integrated into the plug-in hybrid 2 Series Active Tourer, X1, X3, X6, and 7 Series, plus the electric iX3 and i3.

Cars fitted with the latest full-width Panoramic Vision display get a clearer view selection and larger widgets that can be repositioned. What’s more, a upcoming AI avatar function creates a personalized avatar from a photo that the driver can take inside the car using the built-in camera.

Industry observers note that the update also brings the MyMoment Drive Challenge to the iX3 electric SUV. It scores acceleration, braking, and steering, and the results can be seen on the My Trips screen in the My BMW app.

Recent findings suggest that the latest software version will be beamed out to 16 million cars in 88 countries starting in December. BMW mentioned that some vehicles that are running Operating System 8 can be upgraded to 8.5 for free over the air or at the dealer for a fee. The company didn’t detail which cars would be eligible for a free upgrade, though.

The Hyundai IONIQ 3 is now on sale across Europe and the UK as a smaller sibling to the IONIQ 5, positioned between the Inster EV and Hyundai Kona Electric.

The base IONIQ 3 Advance trim with the 42 kWh battery starts at £18,495 ($25,000) OTR and offers up to 213 miles of WLTP range. That’s including the UK’s £3,750 Electric Car Grant.

The IONIQ 3 Advance with the 61 kWh battery starts at £21,995 ($29,000) and offers a “class-leading” WLTP range of up to 308 miles. That also includes the UK government ECG grant.

Unlike the larger IONIQ 5, the IONIQ 3 uses a 400V architecture. However, the 42 kWh battery can still recharge from 10% to 80% in about 29 minutes. The 61 kWh battery takes around 30 minutes.

In Germany and other European markets, Hyundai’s compact IONIQ 3 starts at about €28,950 ($33,000).

#132499. ‘Root-to-Tip’ Eating: Are You Missing Out on Fiber by Discarding Scraps?

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (829 w)

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Healthline ↗ Open Full Page

‘Root-to-Tip’ Eating: Are You Missing Out on Fiber by Discarding Scraps?

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (829 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Healthline

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Eating fruit and veggie scraps may boost fiber intake and cut food waste.
  • This study from King’s College London found that peels, skins, seeds, and stalks of fruits and vegetables—parts often discarded—contained significantly more dietary fiber than the commonly eaten portions in 10 of 12 produce types analyzed.
  • In some cases, the fiber content was up to five times higher in these “root-to-tip” components.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Eating fruit and veggie scraps may boost fiber intake and cut food waste.

This study from King’s College London found that peels, skins, seeds, and stalks of fruits and vegetables—parts often discarded—contained significantly more dietary fiber than the commonly eaten portions in 10 of 12 produce types analyzed.

In some cases, the fiber content was up to five times higher in these “root-to-tip” components.

It has been revealed that these findings, recently published in the International Journal of Food Sciences and Nutrition, are noteworthy, since around 95% of U.S. adults aren’t getting enough fiber. What’s more, around one-fifth of all food produced globally is wasted every year.

The researchers identified 12 fresh produce items that were deemed suitable for “root-to-tip” inclusion:.

In the laboratory analysis, they measured the dietary fiber content of both the “root-to-tip” components (skins, peels, seeds, stalks) and the parts that people typically eat.

The key findings of the study showed that in 10 of the 12 produce types, the “root-to-tip” components contained more fiber than the parts typically consumed.

However, broccoli stalks contained 28.4% less fiber than the florets that people usually eat, meaning individuals are already consuming the most fiber-rich part.

Most participants in focus groups saw the nutritional value of the “root-to-tip” approach as more of a motivator than its sustainability.

However, these findings show that a “root-to-tip” approach to many fruits and vegetables could not only support higher dietary fiber intake but also reduce food waste.

Kristin Kirkpatrick, president of KAK, Consulting, LLC, and a dietitian at the Cleveland Clinic Department of Wellness & Preventive Medicine, mentioned that the takeaway isn’t to eat every peel or seed, but to look for safe, simple ways to get more fiber from the foods you’re already buying. Kirkpatrick wasn’t involved in the study.

Industry observers note that this applies to some of the plants analyzed in this study, but not all produce. For instance, you can only eat a kiwi that’s peeled. This is still a better choice than no kiwi (or a processed-food snack in its place) at all.

Fiber is notable for promoting health and preventing chronic conditions such as cardiovascular disease, type 2 diabetes, colorectal cancer, and obesity.

Industry observers note that “Fiber does much more than support regular bowel movements. It helps regulate blood sugar, supports beneficial gut bacteria, and certain types of soluble fiber can help lower LDL cholesterol by increasing bile acid elimination,” noted Michelle Routhenstein, a preventive cardiology dietitian at Entirely Nourished, who wasn’t involved in the study.

On average, adults are recommended to get 25–30 grams (or more, depending on age) of fiber daily.

Both nutrition experts told Healthline that people generally aren’t getting enough fiber because of their food options or choices.

“Most likely because individuals are not consuming enough plants, and overconsuming processed and ultra-processed foods which are typically very low in fiber,” said Kirkpatrick. “Simply not eating enough fruits and vegetables or choosing white refined grains over whole grains can be why a person’s diet is lacking fiber.”.

Routhenstein added, “I think it is important that when we talk about fiber we point out that it doesn’t have to mean completely changing how you eat. I encourage people to incorporate fiber-rich ingredients into familiar, culturally meaningful foods they already enjoy.”.

“Start with small increases with foods you enjoy and build gradually to allow your digestive system to adjust.”.

It is vital to always research any upcoming plant parts before eating them, wash thoroughly, and consult a healthcare professional if you have digestive conditions or concerns.

And remember that not all produce scraps are edible or recommended.

“Any dietary change will be dependent on personal preference. Some individuals may not enjoy or may not know how to add components of a plant they are not used to,” said Kirkpatrick.

It has been revealed that she noted that, based on the study’s examples, an easier option might be to add more kiwi peels and seeds. “In fact, kiwi skin is probably the most practical fruit peel to highlight for consumers,” she remarked.

Routhenstein added, “I think there is a knowledge gap that the skins, peels, from the root to the tip are edible and nutritious, so we need to start there.”.

She suggested that one way to start is by eating the skins of apples, pears, and well-scrubbed carrots. Trim and thinly slice broccoli stalks for stir-fries or soups. Sautée beet greens and stems just as you would spinach. Freeze appropriate vegetable trimmings, such as carrot ends and celery leaves, for homemade broth.

“Root-to-tip eating helps reduce food waste by encouraging us to use more of the edible portions of fruits and vegetables rather than discarding them. It also maximizes the nutritional and economic value of the food we purchase while making better use of the water, land, and energy required to produce it,” said Routhenstein.

“The key is finding simple, enjoyable ways to incorporate these parts into meals we already eat.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the next time you hit the slopes, you might see one of ChargePoint’s EV chargers either in the ski resort’s parking lot or directly at the base of the ski run.
  • Effective immediately, the partnership puts Kässbohrer’s clients, which range from ski resort operators to public parking operators, in direct contact with ChargePoint, which builds the hardware and software for its EV charging network.
  • As a result, ski resorts and indoor ski facilities can get access to an entire charging ecosystem for electric snow groomers and other electric vehicles that may be in a company’s fleet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the next time you hit the slopes, you might see one of ChargePoint’s EV chargers either in the ski resort’s parking lot or directly at the base of the ski run. That’s because the charging network and electric vehicle supply equipment (EVSE) manufacturer has partnered with Kässbohrer, the maker of the iconic PistenBully slope groomer.

Effective immediately, the partnership puts Kässbohrer’s clients, which range from ski resort operators to public parking operators, in direct contact with ChargePoint, which builds the hardware and software for its EV charging network.

As a result, ski resorts and indoor ski facilities can get access to an entire charging ecosystem for electric snow groomers and other electric vehicles that may be in a company’s fleet.

Industry observers note that "Electrification is reaching heavy-duty vehicles that operate under some of the toughest conditions anywhere," mentioned John Saffrett, EVP and Managing Director, Europe at ChargePoint. "Kässbohrer is trusted by ski resorts and fleet operators around the world. Together, we're helping customers electrify entire operations, from snow groomers to public parking, while reducing emissions, improving energy management, and lowering operating costs.".

As luck would have it, Kässbohrer happens to build an all-electric snow groomer, so the partnership goes both ways. ChargePoint gets to sell more chargers, while Kässbohrer gets to sell more electric snow groomers.

The PistenBully 100 E packs a massive 196-kilowatt-hour battery pack rated at 800 volts, which enables a three-hour runtime for the 7-tonne tracked EV. That’s adequate for small to moderately long ski slopes, but for longer slopes, a quick recharge may be needed, and here’s where ChargePoint’s expertise comes into play.

Industry observers note that according to Kässbohrer, the first-ever electric PistenBully can accept up to 150 kW from a DC fast charger, with roughly one hour needed to get the battery from zero to full. With its 268-horsepower, 10,939-pound-foot electric powertrain, the 100 E can drive at up to 17 miles per hour.

"With the PistenBully 100 E, emission-free slope grooming has arrived on the mountain, mentioned Tim Estelmann, Product Manager at Kässbohrer. “But for it to function reliably and sustainably, the right infrastructure is essential. Only when the vehicle and charging solution work together does a powerful machine become a system that operators can rely on day after day and night after night. That is precisely why we are partnering with ChargePoint, together creating the foundation for long-term operational efficiency and sustainability.".

In a recent development, kässbohrer also sells a series hybrid diesel-electric snow groomer that pairs a Cummins oil burner with two electric motors. The diesel engine acts as a generator, so it can keep the revs lower compared to conventional diesel snow groomers. Much like the Suzuki Jimny before it, the Toyota Land Cruiser FJ is a lovable little off-roader that combines cartoonishly tiny proportions with an actual body-on-frame design. Unfortunately for us American enthusiasts, the Land Cruiser FJ also follows the Jimny in not actually being available Stateside. That makes it all the more frustrating to learn that Japanese buyers can get their hands on an FJ with an aftermarket lift for under $32,000, as brought to broader attention by Motor1.

It has been revealed that that price comes from Kuhl Racing, a provider of body kits and other customization elements for a wide variety of cars. The manufacturer is imagining all kinds of ways to transform the Land Cruiser FJ, including lift kits, superchargers, and clearance-focused bumpers that should increase approach and departure angles.

According to recent reports, the most interesting offering is a complete package combining the lift kit with 18-inch wheels and all-terrain tires for just under 5 million yen, or about $31,500 USD. That comes out to more than $10,000 below the American starting price of the most basic possible Toyota 4Runner. The intricacies of the global auto market mean that prices cannot really be compared apples-to-apples across two different markets, but the lifted FJ would still likely come in somewhere below Toyota’s current range of mid-sized off-roaders in America.

Toyota has not revealed any plans to sell the Land Cruiser FJ in America, so the idea of actually buying one of these and installing one of these kits remains just a dream for now. With the Suzuki Jimny similarly unavailable, American buyers looking for the smallest possible off-roader will have to settle for a two-door Jeep Wrangler or Ford Bronco.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Former Valve writer Chet Faliszek – the one behind the likes of Half-Life 2, Portal and its sequel, Team Fortress 2, Left 4 Dead, and even Counter-Strike: Global Offensive – thinks GTA 6 is great… because you choose how to play. A fact that's lost on players complaining about optional missions.

In a recent development, the new Grand Theft Auto is smashing records left, right, and center as the highest-rated game of all time on Metacritic and, as per Sony, the "biggest launch in PlayStation history" to date. However, there's still a vocal (minority, I'd like to think) group of players dismissing it as a game that forces some sort of agenda upon you. Faliszek covers this in his YouTube video on the "moral yellow paint," so to speak, of GTA 6.

According to the Valve veteran, there's no real reason for folks to complain about menial tasks like painting the house as Jason or buying flowers, even if "the game says you're getting some kind of points or… gives you this list.".

While other games use yellow paint to give you set boundaries to stay within, in GTA 6 you can stray in whatever direction you'd like and play how you wish.

Recent findings suggest that in Faliszek's case, that means, uh, "bringing back bodies" and filling the house with corpses. It's all just GTA, after all.

"Now, would I do that in normal life? Does that make me a horrible person? Maybe. Does that make me a psycho in the game? Who cares?" As he says, "This is Grand Theft Auto." So, go on and ditch the chores to commit mass murder (if you please, of course). The writer notes that, again, it's all part of the game's sandbox elements – and, on that point, part of what makes Grand Theft Auto 6 such a stand-out release.

In a separate short, Faliszek dubs GTA 6 "a masterpiece," saying, "it may be the greatest game ever made." He references other devs' criticism of Rockstar's newly introduced title – such as Warren Spector's, which argues he'd "rather have hundreds of games and full employment" – and dismisses it, reiterating that "it's an amazing game" and "incredible." I'm sure the freedom (to collect bodies, apparently) is a major reason why.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

So, share in Faliszek's sentiment here and don't box yourself in with any preconceived "yellow paint" in GTA 6 when you don't have to. Clean the house, shower, buy gifts… or wreak havoc in Vice City and kill everyone in sight. The choice is yours.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.
  • It has been revealed that there’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that the Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

It has been revealed that there’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a latest world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

Ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

It has been revealed that speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a new Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

At the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

According to recent reports, swordsmanship is the upcoming 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

In a recent development, then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the latest regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of latest careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

The aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

Of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

In November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing new free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

It has been revealed that while you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free patch, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • The EREV is Toyota’s fifth “electrified” vehicle, a term that now spans pure electric vehicles (EVs), plug-in hybrids (PHEVs), hybrids (HEVs), and fuel-cell electric vehicles (FCEVs).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Toyota is set to reveal its first extended-range electric vehicle (EREV) on November 27, and from the first look, it could be based on its flagship Highlander SUV.

The EREV is Toyota’s fifth “electrified” vehicle, a term that now spans pure electric vehicles (EVs), plug-in hybrids (PHEVs), hybrids (HEVs), and fuel-cell electric vehicles (FCEVs).

Unlike fully electric vehicles, an EREV also uses a gas engine that serves as a generator to recharge the battery when it gets low, thereby extending the driving range.

EREVs use a smaller battery than a pure electric vehicle, while the engine is typically smaller than a PHEV. While they are quieter and often cheaper than a plug-in, EREVs are also less efficient than a pure EV.

A Nikkei report in September claimed that Toyota was preparing to begin production of its first EREV in China in Spring 2027.

It appears the rumors are true. Toyota’s joint venture in China, GAC Toyota, posted a preview on its Weibo account with the caption #Toyota doesn’t rush but range-extended.

Recent findings suggest that toyota didn’t confirm the name, but all signs point to it being the Highlander EREV. The blurry preview looks like the Highlander, and when translated into English, a part of the text below it reads “Cash in on the classics. Global flagship SUV. Not a quick fix, but a range extender.”.

Industry observers note that GAC Toyota will reveal the fresh EREV at the Guangzhou Motor Show on November 27. Check back for the full details.

According to the Nikkei report, Toyota aims to produce 200,000 EREVs in 2027. In 2028, it expects production to double to around 400,000 units.

While Toyota likely won’t bring the extended-range EV to the US, it is set to launch the fully electric version of its three-row Highlander in early 2027 (shown above on the left).

Industry observers note that the all-electric Toyota Highlander BEV will be available with front-wheel-drive and all-wheel-drive powertrains with two battery packs: 77 kWh or 95.8 kWh. The smaller (77 kWh) battery provides up to 287 miles of range, while the larger (95.8 kWh) battery provides up to 320 miles in FWD models.

Inside, the electric Toyota Highlander EV offers three rows of seating with room for up to seven passengers.

The three-row electric SUV will be built at Toyota’s manufacturing plant in Georgetown, Kentucky.

Like most foreign brands, Toyota is struggling to keep up with domestic brands like BYD, Geely, and Chery in China’s brutal auto market.

However, it’s Toyota’s gas and hybrid cars that are getting crushed by the competition. In the first nine months of 2026, Toyota sold just over 1.05 million vehicles in China, about 19% fewer than in the same period last year.

After sales plunged nearly 20%, marking its eighth consecutive month with lower year-over-year sales, Toyota noted the market in China “remained weak due in part to rising gasoline prices, while the market for gasoline vehicles and hybrid vehicles was particularly affected.”.

Recent findings suggest that meanwhile, BYD introduces a self-driving SUV with 600 miles of range that recharges in 10 minutes. These guys are toast.

Toyota looks to avoid the intensifying price war with pure electric vehicles in China. An EREV can potentially be offered at a premium, especially as a flagship SUV.

A organization executive said (via Nikkei) that “Competition in China is intensifying as the market fixates on battery EVs, leading to price wars among automakers,” adding, “We need to take steps to avoid being dragged into that competition.”.

Will an EREV help power Toyota’s comeback in China? Or is it late to the party once again? Share your thoughts in the comments.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sporty cars face a conundrum with their steering wheels. A thick steering wheel and giant paddle shifters are very handy when wielding the car at its limits on track, but that same wheel can be annoying and cumbersome overkill for an everyday commute ... which, let’s face it, is what most people are doing with their BMW M vehicles.

Industry observers note that porsche, however, has a potential solution to the problem—one guaranteed to generate all kinds of puerile puns. As website CarMoses recently uncovered, a recent German patent filing from Porsche provides details for a shape-shifting steering wheel, which can enlarge and reduce the thickness of its rim at the push of a button.

According to recent reports, the patented Porsche steering wheel contains two elements. One is a hydraulic system that expands and deflates certain sections of the wheel rim for enhanced grip; a stretchy Alcantara material would accommodate the wheel’s, er, tumescence. The other element is paddle shifters on either spoke that would expand when needed in concert with the wheel, and retract when not in use. When deployed, the system would give the driver greater contact patch for their hands during aggressive driving, be it steering or shifting.

Industry observers note that the wheel rim and paddle shifters could deploy automatically by shifting into a sporty driving mode, or manually with the push of a button. Drivers wishing for their Porsche to appear happy to see them could also have the wheel thickening deploy through a pre-set driver profile. The patent also notes that the wheel rim’s hydraulic system could have an additional temperature-regulation function; it could double as a heater for the wheel in cold weather, or cool the wheel on track.

It has been revealed that keep in mind, automakers patent many features that are unlikely to make it to production. (Don’t expect to drive standing up in your Ford Bronco anytime soon.) But the expanding and retracting steering wheel feels like it could be useful in future Porsches, if the brand can work out safety concerns and add it in a reasonably cost-effective manner. That remarked, the feature would, alas, provide a clear visual indicator that would make slyly slipping the car into a sportier driving mode on a curvy road while your partner isn’t paying attention a bit more difficult to hide.

Latest Update: Winter Weather Hits EV Range Hard. One Automaker Handles It Better Than Tesla

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that with the first signs of winter making their presence felt in some regions, it’s handy to remember that electric cars lose range when temperatures drop considerably.
  • This year, Tesla has been dethroned in the automaker rankings by an unexpected competitor, though the American EV manufacturer still holds the first two spots when it comes to individual models.
  • Polestar, the Swedish-headquartered, Chinese-owned company that’s no longer allowed to sell cars in the United States after its inventory dries up, surpassed Tesla in the EV winter range rankings.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that with the first signs of winter making their presence felt in some regions, it’s handy to remember that electric cars lose range when temperatures drop considerably. It happens across the board, but some automakers and models handle the cold better than others, and a fresh study of over 59,000 EVs from Recurrent shows which battery-powered cars retain the most range when the thermometer reaches 32°F (0°C).

This year, Tesla has been dethroned in the automaker rankings by an unexpected competitor, though the American EV manufacturer still holds the first two spots when it comes to individual models.

Polestar, the Swedish-headquartered, Chinese-owned company that’s no longer allowed to sell cars in the United States after its inventory dries up, surpassed Tesla in the EV winter range rankings. The company’s models retain, on average, 88% of their range at 32°F (0°C) compared to ideal conditions, and 83% when the thermometer reads 20°F (-7°C).

Polestar 2 Arctic Circle Collection.

Meanwhile, Tesla, which has historically been the top performer in Recurrent’s rankings because of its early investments in heat pump systems and other winter optimizations, is second on the list this year, with an 85% average range retention at 32°F (0°C) and 77% at 20°F (-7°C).

Audi completes the automaker podium, with the German marque’s EVs retaining 79% of their range at 32°F (0°C) and 71% at 20°F (-7°C), according to Recurrent.

At this point, it’s worth noting that the comparison point for these figures is not the official EPA range figure, but the longest range achieved by a particular EV in ideal conditions, as recorded by Recurrent’s system. As a reminder, the tech giant gathers real-world data from EVs through owners who are willing to connect their cars to Recurrent’s servers.

According to recent reports, this year, Toyota is at the bottom of the list, with its EVs retaining just 70% of their summer range at freezing temperatures, with Mercedes-Benz not far ahead. Rivian ranked sixth, with an average range retention of 78% at 32°F (0°C), ahead of Hyundai and Porsche, but below Jaguar and Nissan.

When looking at individual electric models, Tesla still has the lead, with the heat pump-equipped Model S ranking first. The discontinued electric sedan retains 90% of its summer range at 32°F (0°C), followed by the soon-to-be-discontinued Cybertruck, with an average retention rate of 89%.

Despite Tesla losing to Polestar in the overall rankings, the Model S still has the lead in the models list.

Industry observers note that next up is the Polestar 2, the entry-level sedan that put Polestar on the map. The four-door EV can still deliver 88% of its summer range at 32°F (0°C), followed by the Tesla Model X with 87% and the Tesla Model 3 with 85%.

The popular Hyundai Ioniq 5 is 10th on the list, with an average range retention rate of 81%, below the Ioniq 6, Audi e-tron GT, Tesla Model Y, and Chevrolet Silverado EV, but above the Audi e-tron, Rivian R1S, and Nissan Ariya.

Sources indicate that the pre-facelift Toyota bZ4X is at the bottom of the list with 70% of range available when the temperature is 32°F (0°C), ahead of the Mercedes-Benz EQS, Chevrolet Blazer EV, Mercedes-Benz EQS SUV, and Cadillac Lyriq. Interestingly, the Volkswagen e-Golf, which is over two decades old and doesn’t have a battery thermal management system, ranked above Cadillac’s Lyriq.

Sources indicate that on average, the 43 electric models included in Recurrent’s dataset retain 78% of their range in freezing temperatures compared to ideal conditions. That noted, the best EVs out there top out at 90% range retention, while the bottom of the pack gets only 70%.

Recent findings suggest that A heat pump makes a world of difference when it comes to boosting winter range. Compared to traditional resistive heating systems, an EV equipped with a heat pump will have 8% more range in the winter, which can make the difference between getting home and calling a tow truck.

Speaking of home, home charging and preconditioning the car’s interior before setting off will also preserve precious miles when it’s time to go somewhere with a thick coat on. By using electricity from the grid to heat up the cabin, the battery will last longer before needing a recharge.

#132487. Tesla quietly sets up a organization at German machine maker EMAG’s HQ

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (988 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Tesla quietly sets up a organization at German machine maker EMAG’s HQ

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (988 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla has registered a new German manufacturer whose business address is the headquarters of EMAG, a struggling machine-tool maker that builds production equipment for the gears inside humanoid robots.
  • Neither organization confirmed a deal.
  • Recent findings suggest that the manufacturer is called Tesla Machining Technologies Management SE.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla has registered a new German manufacturer whose business address is the headquarters of EMAG, a struggling machine-tool maker that builds production equipment for the gears inside humanoid robots.

Neither organization confirmed a deal. But the paper trail is hard to ignore, and it lines up neatly with Tesla’s push to mass-produce Optimus.

Recent findings suggest that the manufacturer is called Tesla Machining Technologies Management SE. Germany’s official company register lists it under HRB 315756 at the Munich district court, with €120,000 in share capital and a business address of Austraße 24 in Salach, a small town east of Stuttgart. That’s EMAG’s home base.

Industry observers note that it didn’t start out as a Tesla company. The register highlights it was first entered on August 26 as “Blitz 26-299 SE,” a shell company. Law firms sell these pre-registered shells so buyers can skip weeks of incorporation paperwork, and Tesla renamed this one earlier this month.

Business Insider Germany, which reported the change based on a notice in the federal gazette, states three people run it: Maximilian Stromberger, Tesla Germany’s 33-year-old head of sales, an American robotics engineer, and the head of HR at Tesla’s Grünheide factory.

In a recent development, the HR chief is the interesting name. You don’t need one to hold a passive stake in a supplier, but you do if you’re about to take on employees.

Neither Tesla nor EMAG answered Business Insider’s repeated requests for comment.

Local press near Salach has been on this for over a week. On November 23, the Stuttgarter Nachrichten reported that signs of a Tesla entry were piling up and that EMAG had briefed its workforce at a large staff meeting the week before. Business Insider dates that meeting to November 16.

Today, the same paper went further. It reports that around 220 EMAG employees will move to Tesla, that the two companies have been working together for some time, and that the deal is about humanoid robots. The full story is paywalled, and none of it has been confirmed by either tech giant.

EMAG, with roots going back to 1867, makes turning, grinding, and gear-cutting machines, mostly for car parts like transmissions and drivetrains. The auto slowdown hit it hard. A year ago, EMAG mentioned it would cut 455 jobs in Germany, roughly 300 of them in Salach, which is about a third of its domestic staff. It lost €42 million on €496 million of revenue in 2024, per Business Insider. It has been talking to potential investors ever since.

It has been revealed that but EMAG has also been chasing a latest market. Its website has an entire section on manufacturing humanoid robot actuator parts: flexsplines, wave generators, and planetary gears.

The first two make up a strain wave gear, the compact, high-reduction gearbox used in robot joints. Planetary gears go in the bigger joints that carry more load. EMAG claims its machines hold these parts to ISO 1328 Class 4 gear quality, with runout under 5 micrometers, and can repeat that in high-volume production.

That’s right where Tesla indicates it’s stuck. On the Q3 earnings call last month, Musk called the hand Optimus’ main hardware problem and flagged custom gears as a reliability worry, as we reported at the time. Tesla is installing a Fremont line designed for a million robots a year, and the Optimus design it highlighted in 2022 used 28 structural actuators per robot. At that volume, you’re talking about tens of millions of actuators a year, many of them built around precision gears that few suppliers can make consistently.

Tesla moving directly into precision tooling highlights a brutal reality for robotics founders: software gets the spotlight, but high-tolerance actuator supply chains dictate your unit economics and scale. Building physical AI means mastering industrial manufacturing long before mass production begins. When navigating high-stakes hardware trade-offs and specialized talent, having early backers who have built hardware companies matters. Grove Ventures works hands-on from pre-seed with deeptech and AI founders, offering real operator experience to help scale complex physical architectures.

Tesla is already building the German side of this. In July, Tesla started recruiting in Reutlingen to develop and manufacture Optimus parts, including sensors, gearboxes, and actuators, plus the equipment to mass-produce them. Reutlingen is the former Manz site that Tesla took over in early 2025, along with about 300 of its employees.

Tesla has done this before. It agreed to buy Grohmann Engineering in Prüm in late 2016, which became Tesla Automation, and that unit absorbed the Manz operations. Tesla is also putting €3 billion into a Cybercab factory at Giga Berlin.

According to recent reports, tesla briefly acquired Wiferion in Germany. Tesla did buy the wireless charging startup in 2023, but it sold the business a few months later and kept the engineers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in 1941, General Motors hit the open road with its fleet of Futureliners on the Parade of Progress, a movement meant to spread cutting-edge science and technology across America. With their bubble-top cockpits, exhibition-style innards, and shining chrome panels, the Futureliners became as much of a spectacle as the displays on automotive technology, urban engineering, farming, and leisure pursuits carried within. Now, 85 years later, a resurrected Futureliner is carrying the Parade of Progress torch into the 21st Century—starting in New York City.

According to recent reports, like many modern automotive stories, this Futureliner's resurrection began on Facebook Marketplace. When Matt Katz, owner of the Caretakers Collection, was sent a link to an available Futureliner on the online classified site, he jumped into action. Katz was on the phone with the seller in a matter of minutes, and quickly deputized friend and Upcoming Jersey car builder Rob Ida to travel up to Massachusetts the following day.

“[The seller] was totally caught off guard that I just called him. He's like, ‘Listen, like it's Monday night. I'm out at an event. You know, call me tomorrow.’ I'm like, ‘No, no, no, I want to make this deal now.’ I just wanted to lock it up,” Katz stated to Road & Track. He said he informed the seller that he wanted Ida, with whom Katz had done prior restoration projects, to come check out the Futureliner. “I was like, ‘Let me call [Ida] and get him to come out and inspect it within forty-eight hours. And if all is good, I'll wire you the balance. And if all is not, return the money to me, the deposit, and we'll call it even.’”.

According to recent reports, ida reported back that the Futureliner example was ripe for restoration, but the journey couldn’t begin immediately. First, Ida had to cut a larger opening in his garage to fit the Futureliner through. Standing 11-feet-7-inches tall and 33 feet long, the GM Futureliner is taller than your average school bus, and about as long as an average fire truck. But once the Futureliner had been transported and maneuvered into Ida’s garage, the real work began.

As it had been owned and restored by the Peter Pan Bus Company in the 1990s, this Futureliner build started out in better shape than most. It had been updated with GM’s post-World War II styling from 1953—a flatter and less regal version of the shape introduced in 1939. Ida and Katz wanted to bring this Futureliner back to its original Harley Earl-designed glory, but there wasn’t an official blueprint to guide them. Ida even reached out to the General Motors Heritage Center, but it had limited information available about the first-generation Futureliner design. So, Ida had to fabricate many of the parts himself. Some era-specific parts even required the creation of bespoke molds, as no replacements were available.

“We work off imagery, and we work off of any kind of text or information that we can find. Unfortunately, the Thirty-Nine version is much more difficult to find than the Fifty-Three version. Anytime you do a quick search, you're going to find all the white roof Fifty-Three generation-two post-war Futureliner. So that was really the difficult part: digging deep enough to find the Thirty-Nine version,” Ida said to Road & Track.

It has been revealed that “Somewhere in a conversation with Rob, it came to be that we both agreed: let's go back to the bubble. Let's bring it back to Thirty-Nine, and we didn't realize and truly fully appreciate what that meant. Getting the bubble done was just difficult, but we knew what to do, and Rob had experience,” Katz said. “We didn't realize that after we made that decision, everything else would change on the bus. Not just the paint colors, but also the cladding on the side. So, Fifty-Three has seven clads; ours is four. The GM logo on the front. Rob randomly found this old video by a production firm called Rose that I discovered, and he poured through it and discovered in a small clip that the GM logo was backlit.”.

Once the restoration was complete, Katz and Ida were eager to show off the piece of moving history, and the inaugural Retromobile event in Fresh York City was the perfect venue. But the newly revived Futureliner had to make it from Old Bridge, New Jersey, to Manhattan’s Jacob K. Javits Convention Center. There is no shortage of driving obstacles between those two points on a good day in a regular car, so piloting the massive machine was sure to be a challenge—but with Ida and Katz at the helm, however, the journey went smoother than expected. Thanks to dually-style front wheels, power steering, 360-degree cameras, and working air conditioning, driving the Futureliner was an exercise in patience more than anything else.

“So I drove from Columbus Circle to Times Square to Javits. And as a Upcoming Yorker, driving it in New York and just seeing people's reactions ... you know, part of the enjoyment is how people react to it. I've never had a reaction like when I was driving it. And then the fact that they closed Times Square for me while we were driving, and for Rob and me ... I couldn't even have fathomed that as a dream,” Katz stated.

And the Futureliner’s adventures are far from over. Katz and Ida are right now scheming a cross-country road trip, starting on the East Coast in 2027 and heading west toward GM’s Heritage Center in Sterling, Michigan. After that, the Futureliner will head to California for the 2027 Pebble Beach Concours d’Elegance, with stops at dealerships and historical markers along the way. The Futureliner will then spend some time at the Petersen Automotive Museum in Los Angeles and stick around for the 2028 Summer Olympics before heading back to GM’s Heritage Center. This cross-country journey will be focused on charity efforts for organizations like the Sloan Kettering Institute for Cancer Research, which the original Parade of Progress highlighted. Trust us: if the Futureliner comes to your town, it’s worth seeing in person.

The woes of alternate side parking have kept his fleet moderate, with a 2014 Volkswagen Jetta GLI and a BMW 318i E30 street parked in his Queens community.

Inside the Hot Wheels Design Center

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1499 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popsci

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The most incredible toy store on Earth—Mattel’s Handler Team Center, the company’s design hub tucked away on a nondescript stretch of road in El Segundo, California—is all these things and more.
  • From a giant mural, Mattel’s cofounders, Elliot and Ruth Handler, smile down on the building’s front lobby, where life-size Hot Wheels vehicles appear poised for action, and wall art displays iconic Mattel playsets and characters from the tech giant’s inception through the present day.
  • In a recent development, there’s speed (the cars reach what would equate to 297 mph at full scale), experimentation (do you go with a weightier or sleeker car?), and crashes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

State-of-the-art car garage. Museum. Mad scientist’s lab. Stuntworks. The most incredible toy store on Earth—Mattel’s Handler Team Center, the company’s design hub tucked away on a nondescript stretch of road in El Segundo, California—is all these things and more.

From a giant mural, Mattel’s cofounders, Elliot and Ruth Handler, smile down on the building’s front lobby, where life-size Hot Wheels vehicles appear poised for action, and wall art displays iconic Mattel playsets and characters from the tech giant’s inception through the present day. Down at the very far end of the lobby, the Epic Loop screams for attention. It is an eleven-foot-tall Hot Wheels duo racetrack with side-by-side loops. Visitors are encouraged to re-create a game played by millions of young Hot Wheels fans by climbing a flight of stairs and sending a die-cast car of their choice down the competing tracks in a race to launch their car into a bucket that marks the finish line.

In a recent development, there’s speed (the cars reach what would equate to 297 mph at full scale), experimentation (do you go with a weightier or sleeker car?), and crashes. Lots of crashes.

The message is clear: This place is a temple of wild design and outrageous fun.

Push deeper into the 200,000-square-foot building (which once housed an aerospace manufacturer), and you arrive at the beating heart of the world’s most famous brand on four wheels: the Hot Wheels Design Center.

Every inch of this place is filled with reminders of Hot Wheels’ storied past, as well as the schematics and prototypes that map out its high-tech future.

Oh, and there are toy cars. Everywhere. Toy cars on tables, toy cars in pristine display cases fit for the Louvre, smashed-up toy cars piled in cluttered cubicles. It’s every kid’s and every collector’s dream come true—as well as a dream come true for the people working inside these walls.

The Hot Wheels die-cast design team sits together in a ring, their cubicles surrounding long tables that serve as a communal space for collaboration, display, tinkering, and sharing the occasional Friday morning donut.

According to recent reports, black light-blocking hoods arch over each cubicle, giving them the feeling of a custom car garage or the messiest kid’s bedroom ever. Within the cubicles, toy cars in every stage of design are piled up against keyboards, and the interior cube walls are plastered with pinned-up artwork, schematics, and toy racks.

Recent findings suggest that underneath one of these hoods sits Dwayne Vance, a longtime Hot Wheels designer who is now manager of product design and steers the visual direction of every graphic in die-cast for Hot Wheels. Vance has worked for other huge brands like DC Comics, EA Games, and Texaco, and his passion for art and automotive extends well beyond the walls of this place, from his creation and curation of art shows to his own book series, Masters of Chicken Scratch, devoted to futuristic and fantasy hot-rod artwork and designs.

Sources indicate that an oversize rendering he created in the early 2000s of the Hot Wheels classic car Bone Shaker, with the word Attitude boldly emblazoned across the top, hangs over his work area. Unlike many of his fellow designers, Vance’s cubicle is neatly arranged and organized. “It helps me creatively to sit down in a nice clean space,” he claims. Some of his favorite cars fill his shelves, as does his Matty Award.

According to recent reports, every designer has particular strengths, so when Hot Wheels decided it was time to breathe fresh life into the Custom Camaro, Vance was part of a small group of designers tasked with cooking up new concepts. “We wanted a licensed vehicle but with an extreme custom,” says Staff Product Designer Fraser Campbell. “Knowing Dwayne’s work, I knew he’d create something wild.”.

As pens hit paper in a flurry of ideas, the designers soon faced a challenge not uncommon for Hot Wheels: the ticking clock. Campbell explains that when putting together a year’s lineup for initial concept review (ICR), where the cars get evaluated and refined to ensure a good overall mix before things move along to production, the designers need to fill in any perceived gaps—promptly.

“Several of us designers were going to be working on the Camaro, but the other guys got so busy that it was up to me to finish the project,” says Vance. “So, I was like, ‘Okay, cool!’ I got to spend maybe two weeks on the design—it wasn’t a lot. One thing we don’t have here is the luxury of time.”.

But just like race car drivers behind the wheels of the cars they’re inspired by, Hot Wheels designers thrive under pressure.

Sources indicate that vance began where he always begins—sketching. “I usually just go straight to Photoshop. I have a monitor on my desk, and I actually sketch right on the monitor,” he explains. But the motor muse can strike at any time and any place, and in the case of this redesign, it hit Vance at thirty thousand feet.

It has been revealed that “I was on a plane and pulled out my sketchbook and put down some initial ideas,” he states. He typically has a sketchbook within reach, but any piece of paper will do. “Sometimes I’ll draw a little piece of a car on a sticky note,” he says.

Whenever the muse speaks, he listens—and gives it a soundtrack with the help of a little music and his headphones. “I listen to a lot of deep house when I’m drawing in my cube,” he says. “It’s got good energy and is easy to draw to.”.

For the 2023 Custom ’68 Camaro reboot, Vance aimed to commemorate the past while bringing it into the future, inspired by what he saw happening in modern muscle-car culture. Instead of trying to restore vintage rides to their original settings, he saw customizers on a mission to “make muscle cars beautiful again” with newly introduced engines, new suspensions, and new brake systems—“they were just chopping them up.”.

Vance studied the work of boundary-pushing, high-end car builders like Hoonigan, and when he saw a ’69 Mustang that a customizer had retrofitted with an LS1 Corvette engine, a vision began to crystallize.

“I thought, how fun would it be to do that to the Camaro?”.

He broke out the chop saw in his mind and went to town, cutting out body panels to reveal the exhaust system sticking out of the side of the car. He lopped off the whole front bumper, exposing much of the car’s underpinnings. He added a recessed grille with an air intake, and in keeping with the Hot Wheelizing philosophy of pushing the limits while keeping it recognizable, he stayed true to the Camaro’s signature headlight shape.

Vance also created a hood bulge that hints at the powerful engine underneath and bolted on vertical fins in the back, inspired by the Le Mans Prototype (LMP) race cars used in endurance racing. “The fins help these race cars with cornering, giving them friction so they can stay grounded and accelerate. I thought, let’s add that to a muscle car!”.

He then hacked off the rear bumpers to expose the roll cage, which he says, “really did something ultra-aggressive to the car.”.

When it came time to create the 2026 Custom ’68 Camaro for this book, Vance again engaged in some role-playing—but this time he stepped into the shoes of someone with a very different perspective from a cyberpunk racer.

“I put myself in the Hot Wheels collector’s position—I wanted something that really celebrates the brand and yells, ‘Hot Wheels!’”.

To that end, Vance gave his punked-up ’23 model a sleek latest paint and decoration job. The base color is a rich Spectraflame red; the side panels are emblazoned with big Hot Wheels flames; the hood declares Hot Wheels loud and proud; and the side panels and roof feature the number 68, a nod to the year Elliot Handler started Hot Wheels. Vance also added classic race wheels typically found on 1960s stock cars to complete what he calls a modernized classic.

“I want a collector to see this and say, ‘Man, I want this book, but I really, really want the car!’”.

He interviews amazing inventors and innovators for Entrepreneur.com and hosts the Get a Real Job podcast. He lives in Fresh York with his wife, two sons, and a completely bonkers dog named Clark.

Recent findings suggest that arknights: Endfield developer Gryphline has a good reason to celebrate, as the upcoming free-to-play action RPG has achieved yet another milestone. The developer revealed today that Endfield already has over 35 million pre-registrations.

This a major moment for the game, which is poised to be one of 2026’s biggest releases on mobile.

In December, when Gryphline officially revealed the Arknights: Endfield release date, the developer remarked at the time that the game had surpassed 30 million pre-registrations, meaning over 5 million more have joined in since then.

Arknights: Endfield has pretty much wrapped up closed testing, and we’re in the final stretch ahead of the January 22 launch, when the free-to-play game will go live across PC (where it'll be available via the Epic Games Store, as well as Gryphline's own launcher), PS5, and mobile platforms (iOS, Android).

The developer hosted a livestream to celebrate, where it also debuted two latest trailers: the launch trailer (below), as well as another look at gameplay. The gameplay trailer also shows off more of the game’s Talos-2 world, and sets up the mystery at the centre of its narrative.

It has been revealed that if you’re going to be playing Endfield on PC, you’ll be happy to know that you can expert a breezy experience with support for 120fps. The game also comes with a wide range of modern technologies, including Nvidia DLSS Super Resolution, and Frame Generation. Both Xbox and PlayStation controllers are supported, too.

You can expect more Arknights: Endfield coverage from us at release and beyond. In fact, based on what we played so far, we’re pretty confident in this early Arknights Endfield characters list.

Warren Spector: "I don't think you can look at Zelda: Breath of the Wild and not see Deus Ex"

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Speaking to Edge, legendary immersive sim designer Warren Spector said that "the heart of the immersive sim has kind of been adopted by mainstream gaming." Best known for series like Thief, System Shock, Ultima, and Deus Ex, Spector is widely considered a major force in the development of the entire imsim genre, and that influence is a major personal marker of success.
  • In a recent development, "One of my egomaniacal success criteria was to have influence.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Plenty of people would have told you that the real-time strategy game began to 'die out' in the late 2000s, a once-mighty genre that no longer interested modern audiences. But the more nuanced version of that narrative is that the RTS evolved, various core ideas stripped of their outside complexities before being expanded into their own genres. Without Warcraft 3, for instance, there wouldn't have been a League of Legends or Dota 2. Now, a leading figure behind another 'dying' genre notes that its DNA is simply to be found elsewhere - primarily within the RPG.

Speaking to Edge, legendary immersive sim designer Warren Spector said that "the heart of the immersive sim has kind of been adopted by mainstream gaming." Best known for series like Thief, System Shock, Ultima, and Deus Ex, Spector is widely considered a major force in the development of the entire imsim genre, and that influence is a major personal marker of success.

In a recent development, "One of my egomaniacal success criteria was to have influence. I've always wanted to try, even if I fail, to change things." His argument, however, is that he has very much not failed to change things, and that the ideas that were once the individual domain of the immersive sim are now found much further afield.

Industry observers note that "I don't think you can look at Breath of the Wild or Tears of the Kingdom and not see a little bit of Deus Ex in it," he says. "And I think roleplaying games now are far more immersive sim-y than they used to be, going further to empower players to tell their own stories." While the two Zelda titans are obvious examples, other RPGs have also done work to deserve that mantle - Baldur's Gate 3 is a particularly good example of the imsim's systems-driven heritage, and a lot of what we're hearing about GTA 6 implies that some of its massive ideas - particularly its Wanted system - will be very immersive.

Sources indicate that the result, for Spector, is that a trace of the old self exists in the new self. Even if immersive sims aren't a driving force in the industry right now, he says, "I don't know that we're dead. I think we're like a parasite that's invaded the body. And that's all you can ask for. Making games different and better and more what they should be, and empowering players to become authors - that's all I ever wanted to do, and now there are lots of people doing that, even if they don't realise they are.".

VW Will Pay German Drivers To Plug In Their EVs. Even If The Grid Never Uses Their Power

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that plug your electric Volkswagen in at 8 in the evening, unplug it at 6 the next morning, and you could earn €2.40 while you sleep.
  • Recent findings suggest that we already wrote about Germany’s plan to allow parked EVs to earn money.
  • Elli will pay €0.24 for each hour the EV is plugged in, provided each session lasts at least three hours.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that plug your electric Volkswagen in at 8 in the evening, unplug it at 6 the next morning, and you could earn €2.40 while you sleep. How much electricity would your car have to send back to the grid for that money? Potentially none. Starting in December, VW’s charging subsidiary Elli will pay eligible German drivers for the hours their car spends plugged in at home, even if it doesn’t actually supply any power during that time.

Recent findings suggest that we already wrote about Germany’s plan to allow parked EVs to earn money. New rules made it easier to account for electricity stored in a car and later sold back to the grid, even for homes that can generate their own power through solar panels. That left a fairly key question for anyone with an EV in the driveway: How much could you actually earn? Now, Volkswagen has put a number on it.

Elli will pay €0.24 for each hour the EV is plugged in, provided each session lasts at least three hours. The bonus tops out at €60 a month, or €720 yearly. Earning the full amount takes 250 hours a month, a little over eight hours a night. In the app, you tell Elli when you need the car and how much charge you want when you leave.

In a recent development, elli will handle charging and discharging around your schedule, but to make this work you need its 11-kilowatt bidirectional charger with vehicle-to-grid (V2G) capability. That costs €1,995 without installation, and your home also needs a compatible smart electricity meter for everything to work. Owners can register now, then check eligibility at launch and get an installation quote before ordering.

The thing is, even if you collect every euro of the first-year bonus, that still leaves €1,275 of the charger’s price to cover, plus whatever the electrician charges to install it.

In a recent development, not all VW EVs have bidirectional charging. It introduced this feature on its European models in 2023, but it says there are around one million eligible EVs in Europe, about a third of which are in Germany. The offer covers Volkswagen, Cupra and Škoda, and the charger supports 400- and 800-volt vehicles, even if the latter is not present in any of the three brands’ vehicles.

Elli says it looks to expand into more European markets in 2027 and offer a separate vehicle-to-home system so owners can save rooftop solar power for use after dark. A one-year trial involving 20 German households logged roughly 85,000 combined charger hours online and more than 6,500 charging and discharging sessions, the company said.

VW calculates that €720 could buy enough electricity to drive an ID.3 Neo nearly 10,000 miles (16,000 km), assuming €0.33 per kWh and the car’s official WLTP consumption. So it may not offset the full cost of the bidirectional charger, but that’s still a lot of free driving for just keeping the car plugged in overnight.

At one point, Top Gear was one of the biggest indicates on television of any sort. It has been a long time since the glory days of Clarkson, Hammond, and May, though, and multiple efforts to revive the BBC’s legendary automotive series have failed to come close to the impact of the original. The show has not been in production since its newest episodes aired in 2022, but a fresh host is about to change that very soon. On Wednesday, the BBC unveiled that celebrity chef Gordon Ramsay is taking over the mantle of Top Gear host starting in 2028. Ramsay will be the first host of the show since production paused after a crash involving then-presenter Freddie Flintoff four years ago.

An announcement from the BBC makes no mention of any potential co-hosts alongside Ramsay, but does add that he will be hosting along with “as yet unnamed co-presenters.” The same announcement quotes BBC Studios Entertainment executive Suzy Lamb as saying that the new Top Gear “won't be a nostalgic reboot" and would instead be a “bold and unmissable new chapter” of the show, lines that suggest a major format change could come with the new host.

While Ramsay is most famous for his career as a chef and host of cooking-related demonstrates, he is also a long-time enthusiast who takes his own cars to the track. He even combined the interests back in 2023, cooking a grilled cheese sandwich in the engine bay of his Aston Martin Valkyrie during a track day. This past weekend, he competed in a celebrity race in Lego Formula 1 cars at the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Fred Smith's love of cars comes from his fascination with auto racing. Unfortunately, that passion led him to daily drive a high-mileage, first-year Porsche Panamera. He is still thinking about the last lap of the 2011 Indianapolis 500.

The 2026 Acura Integra Type S is officially for sale in Japan. That might not seem like big news, considering Honda Motor Tech giant is headquartered in Japan, but the release marks the first Acura-branded vehicle to be exported to the Japanese market. While this is Acura’s first time in Japan, it’s strangely not the Integra’s, which spent a few decades wearing a Honda badge from 1985 to 2006.

It has been revealed that most Acuras are designed and built in the United States and sold throughout North America. The newly introduced Integras for sale in Japan are the same as those sold stateside, meaning they’ll be left-hand-drive anomalies in a predominantly right-hand-drive market.

See all results for fresh 2027 Acura Integra Type S for sale near 48105.

That also means they’ll get the same 320-hp turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-four that we’re quite fond of in the United States. The front-wheel-drive sport compact is only offered with a six-speed manual transmission and features a limited-slip differential, Brembo brakes, and 19-inch wheels wrapped in summer tires. The whole package comes together to reach 60 mph in a brisk 5.1 seconds.

According to recent reports, honda builds every Integra Type S at its assembly plant in Marysville, Ohio, and the engines come from Honda’s Anna Engine Plant, also located in Ohio. Honda began exporting vehicles from Ohio to Japan in 1988 and has shipped nearly 300,000 Hondas to Japan since then.

Industry observers note that honda claims the Teg’s introduction in Japan marks a strong global demand for an enthusiast-centered performance sedan. If the Type S is well-received in the Japanese market, it’s likely that more Acuras could start making their way to Japan in the future. Pricing and the exact number of Integra Type S models available in Japan haven’t been released yet, but considering they’re identical to the Type S models sold on our shores, they’ll likely come in around $56,000.

Tomorrow's Battlefield 6 patch somehow makes jets more useless, improves armor bar visibility in Redsec

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed.
  • Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.
  • Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update. When Battlefield Studios unveiled it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

Sources indicate that the patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a big focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

Sources indicate that the end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

According to recent reports, interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

Recent findings suggest that the other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

And, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Finally, the patch makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

Read on below for the 1.1.3.5 change log.
